cards.s_text: And now, my son, obey my voice in that which I command you: Go to your flock and fetch me two good kids of the goats, and I will make them savoury meat for your father, such as he loves, and you shall bring (it) to your father that he may eat and bless you before Yahuah (God) before he die, and that you may be blessed.”
cards.t_text: Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for your father, such as he loves:

cards.note: Genesis 27:20 — *And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) brought it to me.* Jubilees 26:15 has Jacob give the same answer, crediting Elohim for the quick find.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said: “Because Yahuah (God) your Elohim (God) caused me to find.”
cards.t_text: And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) brought it to me.

cards.note: Genesis 27:22 — *And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.* Jubilees 26:18 quotes the identical line, then adds that the failed perception was “a dispensation from heaven.”
cards.s_text: “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau,” and he discerned him not, because it was a dispensation from heaven to remove his power of perception and Isaac discerned not, for his hands were hairy as (his brother) Esau’s, so that he blessed him.
cards.t_text: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.

cards.note: Genesis 27:23 — *And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him.* Jubilees 26:18 reads this same non-discernment as heaven removing Isaac's perception so the blessing would fall on Jacob.
cards.s_text: “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau,” and he discerned him not, because it was a dispensation from heaven to remove his power of perception and Isaac discerned not, for his hands were hairy as (his brother) Esau’s, so that he blessed him.
cards.t_text: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him.

cards.note: Genesis 27:27 — *And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Yahuah (LORD) hath blessed:* Jubilees 26:22 opens the blessing with the same smell-of-the-field that Yahuah has blessed.
cards.s_text: And he smelled the smell of his raiment, and he blessed him and said: "Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a (full) field which Yahuah (God) has blessed.
cards.t_text: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Yahuah (LORD) has blessed:

cards.note: Genesis 27:28 — *Therefore Elohim (God) give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine:* The dew of heaven and plenty of corn of Jubilees 26:23 is the Genesis blessing word for word.
cards.s_text: And may Yahuah (God) give you of the dew of heaven And of the dew of the earth, and plenty of corn and oil: Let nations serve you, And peoples bow down to you.
cards.t_text: Therefore Elohim (God) give you of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine:

cards.note: Genesis 27:29 — *Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother’s sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.* Jubilees 26:23,24 carries the same nations-serve-you, mother's-sons-bow, cursed/blessed formula.
cards.s_text: And may Yahuah (God) give you of the dew of heaven And of the dew of the earth, and plenty of corn and oil: Let nations serve you, And peoples bow down to you.
cards.t_text: Let people serve you, and nations bow down to you: be lord over your brethren, and let your mother’s sons bow down to you: cursed be every one that curses you, and blessed be he that blesses you.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:20 — *By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.* The faith-blessing the NT reckons to Isaac is the very blessing Jubilees 26:21-24 imparts to Jacob “and to your seed for ever.”
cards.s_text: And Isaac, his father, said to him: “Come near and kiss me, my son.” And he came near and kissed him.
cards.t_text: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.

cards.note: Genesis 27:33 — *And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.* Jubilees 26:28 confirms the same irrevocable verdict: he and all his seed shall be blessed for ever.
cards.s_text: And Isaac was very greatly astonished, and said: “Who is he that has hunted and caught and brought (it) to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him: (and) he shall be blessed, and all his seed for ever.”
cards.t_text: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that has taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.

cards.note: Romans 9:12 — *It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.* Paul reads the Jacob-blessing of Jubilees 26:28 as the standing word of election over the elder Esau and the younger Jacob.
cards.s_text: And Isaac was very greatly astonished, and said: “Who is he that has hunted and caught and brought (it) to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him: (and) he shall be blessed, and all his seed for ever.”
cards.t_text: It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.

cards.note: Romans 9:13 — *As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.* The settled election Jubilees 26:28 records — the blessing fixed on Jacob — is what Paul names Jacob-loved, Esau-hated.
cards.s_text: And Isaac was very greatly astonished, and said: “Who is he that has hunted and caught and brought (it) to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him: (and) he shall be blessed, and all his seed for ever.”
cards.t_text: As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.

cards.note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* The prophet grounds Yahuah's love for Israel in the very Jacob-over-Esau choice Jubilees 26:28 seals.
cards.s_text: And Isaac was very greatly astonished, and said: “Who is he that has hunted and caught and brought (it) to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him: (and) he shall be blessed, and all his seed for ever.”
cards.t_text: I have loved you, says Yahuah (LORD). Yet you say, Wherein have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? says Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,

cards.note: Genesis 27:34 — *And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.* Jubilees 26:29 retells the same great and bitter cry of Esau pleading to be blessed too.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac that he cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry, and said to his father: “Bless me, (even) me also, father.”
cards.t_text: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.

cards.note: Genesis 27:36 — *And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?* Jubilees 26:30 has Esau name the two supplantings — birthright then blessing — in the same words.
cards.s_text: And he said to him: “Your brother came with guile, and has taken away your blessing.” And he said: “Now I know why his name is named Jacob: behold, he has supplanted me these two times: he took away my birth-right, and now he has taken away my blessing.”
cards.t_text: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he has supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he has taken away my blessing. And he said, Have you not reserved a blessing for me?

cards.note: Jubilees 24:3 — *And Jacob said to him: “Sell to me your primogeniture, this birthright and I will give you bread, and also some of this lentil pottage.”* The birthright Esau mourns losing in Jubilees 26:29 he had already sold for pottage in Jubilees' earlier telling.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac that he cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry, and said to his father: “Bless me, (even) me also, father.”
cards.t_text: And Jacob sod lentil pottage, and Esau came from the field hungry. And he said to Jacob his brother: “Give me of this red pottage.” And Jacob said to him: “Sell to me your primogeniture, this birthright and I will give you bread, and also some of this lentil pottage.”

cards.note: Hebrews 12:16 — *Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.* The NT reads the Esau of Jubilees 26:29 as the profane man whose lost blessing began with a despised birthright.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac that he cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry, and said to his father: “Bless me, (even) me also, father.”
cards.t_text: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.

cards.note: Genesis 27:39 — *And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;* Jubilees 26:33 gives the inverse — Esau's dwelling far from the dew — of the same Genesis word over Esau.
cards.s_text: And Isaac answered and said to him: “Behold, far from the dew of the earth shall be your dwelling, And far from the dew of heaven from above.
cards.t_text: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, your dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;

cards.note: Genesis 27:40 — *And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.* Jubilees 26:34 carries the same sword-and-yoke word, adding that shaking the yoke ends in Esau's seed rooted out.
cards.s_text: And by your sword will you live, And you will serve your brother. And it shall come to pass when you become great, And do shake his yoke from off your neck, You will sin a complete sin to death, And your seed will be rooted out from under heaven.”
cards.t_text: And by your sword shall you live, and shall serve your brother; and it shall come to pass when you shall have the dominion, that you shall break his yoke from off your neck.

cards.note: Genesis 27:41 — *And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.* Jubilees 26:35 ends with the identical murderous resolve in Esau's heart.
cards.s_text: And Esau kept threatening Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him, and he said in his heart: “May the days of mourning for my father now come, so that I may slay my brother Jacob.”
cards.t_text: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.

cards.note: Malachi 1:3 — *And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.* The prophet confirms the sentence Jubilees 26:34 pronounces on Esau's seed — his heritage laid waste.
cards.s_text: And by your sword will you live, And you will serve your brother. And it shall come to pass when you become great, And do shake his yoke from off your neck, You will sin a complete sin to death, And your seed will be rooted out from under heaven.”
cards.t_text: And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.

cards.note: Leviticus 27:30 — *And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree, is the LORD’S: it is holy unto Yahuah (LORD).* The Torah engraves as holy the very tithe Jacob vows to Yahuah at Bethel in Jubilees 27:27.
cards.s_text: And Jacob vowed a vow to Yahuah (God), saying: “If Yahuah (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then shall Yahuah (God) be my Elohim (God), and this stone which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, shall be Yahuah (God)’s house, and of all that you give me, I shall give the tenth to you, my Elohim (God).”
cards.t_text: And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree, is the LORD’S: it is holy unto Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Genesis 14:20 — *And blessed be the El Elyon (most high God), which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.* Abraham tithed before Jacob ever did — the tenth Jacob vows in Jubilees 27:27 is the fathers' practice, not a new thing.
cards.s_text: And Jacob vowed a vow to Yahuah (God), saying: “If Yahuah (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then shall Yahuah (God) be my Elohim (God), and this stone which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, shall be Yahuah (God)’s house, and of all that you give me, I shall give the tenth to you, my Elohim (God).”
cards.t_text: And blessed be the El Elyon (most high God), which has delivered your enemies into your hand. And he gave him tithes of all.

cards.note: Genesis 28:17 — *And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of Elohim (God), and this is the gate of heaven.* Jacob's dread and the “gate of heaven” cry of Jubilees 27:25 word for word from Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and said, “Truly this place is the house of Yahuah (God), and I knew it not.” And he was afraid and said:" Dreadful is this place which is none other than the house of Elohim (God), and this is the gate of heaven."
cards.t_text: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of Elohim (God), and this is the gate of heaven.

cards.note: Genesis 28:18 — *And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.* Jubilees 27:26 retells the raising and anointing of the Bethel pillar nearly verbatim.
cards.s_text: And Jacob arose early in the morning, and took the stone which he had put under his head and set it up as a pillar for a sign, and he poured oil upon the top of it. And he called the name of that place Bethel; but the name of the place was Luz at the first.
cards.t_text: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.

cards.note: Genesis 28:15 — *And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.* Jubilees 27:24 carries the promise of presence and safe return word for word from the Bethel vision.
cards.s_text: And behold, I shall be with you, and shall keep you whithersoever you go, and I shall bring you again into this land in peace; for I shall not leave you until I do everything that I told you of.”
cards.t_text: And, behold, I am with you, and will keep you in all places whither you go, and will bring you again into this land; for I will not leave you, until I have done that which I have spoken to you of.

cards.note: Galatians 3:8 — *And the scripture, foreseeing that Elohim (God) would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.* Paul calls the all-families promise of Jubilees 27:23 the gospel preached beforehand — the nations blessed by faith.
cards.s_text: And your seed will be as the dust of the earth, and you will increase to the west and to the east, to the north and the south, and in you and in your seed will all the families of the nations be blessed.
cards.t_text: And the scripture, foreseeing that Elohim (God) would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In you shall all nations be blessed.

cards.note: Genesis 12:2 — *And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:* The first word of the promise to Abraham that Jubilees 27:23 hands down unbroken to Jacob.
cards.s_text: And your seed will be as the dust of the earth, and you will increase to the west and to the east, to the north and the south, and in you and in your seed will all the families of the nations be blessed.
cards.t_text: And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing:

cards.note: Genesis 28:14 — *And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.* Jubilees 27:23 retells the Bethel promise nearly verbatim — the seed as dust and the families blessed.
cards.s_text: And your seed will be as the dust of the earth, and you will increase to the west and to the east, to the north and the south, and in you and in your seed will all the families of the nations be blessed.
cards.t_text: And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in you and in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

cards.note: Genesis 28:11 — *And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.* The stone-pillow at the set of the sun that Jubilees 27:19-20 narrates in its own words.
cards.s_text: And Jacob went from the Well of the Oath to go to Haran on the first year of the second week in the forty-fourth Jubilee, and he came to Luz on the mountains, that is, Bethel, on the new moon of the first month of this week, and he came to the place at even and turned from the way to the west of the road that night: and he slept there; for the sun had set.
cards.t_text: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.

cards.note: John 1:51 — *And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of Elohim (God) ascending and descending upon the Son of Adam.* Yahusha unveils Jacob's ladder of Jubilees 27:21 as Himself — the open heaven and the angels now resting upon the Son of Adam.
cards.s_text: And he dreamt that night, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and behold, the angels of Yahuah (God) ascended and descended on it: and behold, Yahuah (God) stood upon it.
cards.t_text: And he says unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter you shall see heaven open, and the angels of Elohim (God) ascending and descending upon the Son of Adam.

cards.note: Genesis 28:13 — *And, behold, Yahuah (LORD) stood above it, and said, I am Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham thy father, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;* The voice from atop the ladder in Jubilees 27:21 quoting the covenant of the land and the seed.
cards.s_text: And he dreamt that night, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and behold, the angels of Yahuah (God) ascended and descended on it: and behold, Yahuah (God) stood upon it.
cards.t_text: And, behold, Yahuah (LORD) stood above it, and said, I am Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham your father, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac: the land whereon you lie, to you will I give it, and to your seed;

cards.note: Genesis 28:12 — *And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of Elohim (God) ascending and descending on it.* Jubilees 27:21 retells the Bethel dream almost verbatim — the ladder and the ascending-descending angels.
cards.s_text: And he dreamt that night, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and behold, the angels of Yahuah (God) ascended and descended on it: and behold, Yahuah (God) stood upon it.
cards.t_text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of Elohim (God) ascending and descending on it.

cards.note: Genesis 28:5 — *And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padan-aram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.* The sending to Mesopotamia/Padan-aram that Jubilees 27:12 records in its own words.
cards.s_text: And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Mesopotamia, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebecca, Jacob’s mother.
cards.t_text: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padan-aram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

cards.note: Genesis 28:4 — *And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which Elohim (God) gave unto Abraham.* The blessing of Abraham and the inheritance of the land that Jubilees 27:11 hands down to Jacob.
cards.s_text: And El Shaddai (God Almighty) bless you and increase and multiply you that you may become a company of nations, and give you the blessings of my father Abraham, to you and to your seed after you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings and all the land which Elohim (God) gave to Abraham: go, my son, in peace.”
cards.t_text: And give you the blessing of Abraham, to you, and to your seed with you; that you may inherit the land wherein you are a stranger, which Elohim (God) gave unto Abraham.

cards.note: Genesis 28:3 — *And El Shaddai (God Almighty) bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people;* Jubilees 27:11 carries Isaac's El-Shaddai blessing word for word — the company of nations promised to the seed.
cards.s_text: And El Shaddai (God Almighty) bless you and increase and multiply you that you may become a company of nations, and give you the blessings of my father Abraham, to you and to your seed after you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings and all the land which Elohim (God) gave to Abraham: go, my son, in peace.”
cards.t_text: And El Shaddai (God Almighty) bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a multitude of people;

cards.note: Jubilees 30:11 — *And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God).* Jubilees' own self-witness that the seed is kept holy — the covenant-line preserved, the same principle Rebecca pleads in 27:8.
cards.s_text: And Rebecca went in and said to Isaac: “I loathe my life because of the two daughters of Heth, whom Esau has taken him as wives; and if Jacob take a wife from among the daughters of the land such as these, for what purpose do I further live; for the daughters of Canaan are evil.”
cards.t_text: And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:3 — *Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.* The standing Torah law of the seed kept separate that Jubilees 27:10's charge embodies.
cards.s_text: “Do not take you a wife of any of the daughters of Canaan; arise and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother’s father, and take you a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
cards.t_text: Neither shall you make marriages with them; your daughter you shall not give unto his son, nor his daughter shall you take unto your son.

cards.note: Genesis 28:1 — *And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.* Jubilees 27:10 retells Isaac's charge almost word for word — the Genesis source on the page beside it.
cards.s_text: “Do not take you a wife of any of the daughters of Canaan; arise and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother’s father, and take you a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
cards.t_text: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 24:3 — *And I will make thee swear by Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, and the Elohim (God) of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:* The same oath Abraham bound a generation before now drives Rebecca's grief over Esau's Canaanite wives in Jubilees 27:8.
cards.s_text: And Rebecca went in and said to Isaac: “I loathe my life because of the two daughters of Heth, whom Esau has taken him as wives; and if Jacob take a wife from among the daughters of the land such as these, for what purpose do I further live; for the daughters of Canaan are evil.”
cards.t_text: And I will make you swear by Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, and the Elohim (God) of the earth, that you shall not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:

cards.note: Genesis 30:43 — *And the man increased exceedingly, and had much cattle, and maidservants, and menservants, and camels, and asses.* Jubilees 28:29 — “Jacob's possessions multiplied exceedingly” — records the same blessing over Laban's envy.
cards.s_text: And Jacob’s possessions multiplied exceedingly, and he possessed oxen and sheep and asses and camels, and menservants and maidservants.
cards.t_text: And the man increased exceedingly, and had much cattle, and maidservants, and menservants, and camels, and asses.

cards.note: Genesis 30:32 — *I will pass through all thy flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.* The spotted-and-speckled wage of Jubilees 28:27 is Jacob's Genesis bargain.
cards.s_text: And they agreed with one another that he should give him as his wages those of the lambs and kids which were born black and spotted and white, (these) were to be his wages.
cards.t_text: I will pass through all your flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.

cards.note: Hebrews 7:14 — *For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* The kingly tribe born in Jubilees 28:15 is the tribe of the Messiah — Judah's sceptre fulfilled.
cards.s_text: And again Jacob went in to her, and she conceived, and bare him a fourth son, and he called his name Yahudah (Judah), on the fifteenth of the third month, in the first year of the fourth week.
cards.t_text: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.

cards.note: Numbers 24:17 — *...there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.* The Sceptre of Judah's line, first dated at his birth in Jubilees 28:15, is the Star Balaam foresaw.
cards.s_text: And again Jacob went in to her, and she conceived, and bare him a fourth son, and he called his name Yahudah (Judah), on the fifteenth of the third month, in the first year of the fourth week.
cards.t_text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.

cards.note: Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* The Yahudah born in Jubilees 28:15 carries the kingship and the Messianic sceptre.
cards.s_text: And again Jacob went in to her, and she conceived, and bare him a fourth son, and he called his name Yahudah (Judah), on the fifteenth of the third month, in the first year of the fourth week.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 33:8 — *And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one, whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah;* The Levi born in Jubilees 28:14 is the priesthood, the holy one given the Urim and Thummim.
cards.s_text: And again Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived, and bare him a third son, and he called his name Levi, in the new moon of the first month in the sixth year of this week.
cards.t_text: And of Levi he said, Let your Thummim and your Urim be with your holy one, whom you did prove at Massah, and with whom you did strive at the waters of Meribah;

cards.note: Exodus 1:2 — *Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Yahudah (Judah),* The tribe-names born in Jubilees 28 are the same households Exodus carries down into Egypt as the nation Israel.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (God) opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bare Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.
cards.t_text: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Yahudah (Judah),

cards.note: Genesis 35:22 — *...Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:* The births dated through Jubilees 28 — ending with Zebulon and Dinah in v23 — complete the twelve Genesis gathers in one line.
cards.s_text: And Jacob went in again to her, and she conceived, and bare two (children), a son and a daughter, and she called the name of the son Zebulon, and the name of the daughter Dinah, in the seventh of the seventh month, in the sixth year of the fourth week.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when Yashar'el (Israel) dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Yashar'el (Israel) heard it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:

cards.note: Genesis 30:22 — *And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.* Jubilees 28:24 — “Yahuah was gracious to Rachel, and opened her womb” — brings Joseph the same way Genesis does.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (God) was gracious to Rachel, and opened her womb, and she conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year in this fourth week.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

cards.note: Genesis 30:6 — *And Rachel said, Elohim (God) hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.* The handmaid's first son in Jubilees 28:18, Bilhah's Dan, is the same birth Genesis records.
cards.s_text: (And she gave (him) Bilhah her handmaid to wife.) And he went in to her, and she conceived, and bare him a son, and he called his name Dan, on the ninth of the sixth month, in the sixth year of the third week.
cards.t_text: And Rachel said, Elohim (God) has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.

cards.note: Genesis 29:31 — *And when Yahuah (LORD) saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.* Jubilees 28:11 echoes it exactly — “Yahuah saw that Leah was hated and Rachel loved” — as the womb opens for Reuben.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (God) opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bare Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.
cards.t_text: And when Yahuah (LORD) saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.

cards.note: Exodus 32:32 — *Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.* The “book” Moses appeals to is the same heavenly writing Jubilees 28:6 cites — guilt “set down…in heaven,” the law and judgement pre-engraved.
cards.s_text: And Laban said to Jacob: “It is not so done in our country, to give the younger before the elder.” And it is not right to do this; for thus it is ordained and written in the heavenly tables, that no one should give his younger daughter before the elder–but the elder one gives first and after her the younger–and the man who does so, they set down guilt against him in heaven, and none is righteous that does this thing, for this deed is evil before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Yet now, if you will forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray you, out of your book which you have written.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:3 — *Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.* The heavenly-tablet marriage-law Jubilees 28:6 lays on Israel is the same Torah care that the seed be given and kept rightly, not mixed with the nations.
cards.s_text: And Laban said to Jacob: “It is not so done in our country, to give the younger before the elder.” And it is not right to do this; for thus it is ordained and written in the heavenly tables, that no one should give his younger daughter before the elder–but the elder one gives first and after her the younger–and the man who does so, they set down guilt against him in heaven, and none is righteous that does this thing, for this deed is evil before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Neither shall you make marriages with them; your daughter you shall not give unto his son, nor his daughter shall you take unto your son.

cards.note: Genesis 29:26 — *And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.* Jubilees 28:6 takes this bare custom and writes it into the heavenly tables as a binding command to Israel.
cards.s_text: And Laban said to Jacob: “It is not so done in our country, to give the younger before the elder.” And it is not right to do this; for thus it is ordained and written in the heavenly tables, that no one should give his younger daughter before the elder–but the elder one gives first and after her the younger–and the man who does so, they set down guilt against him in heaven, and none is righteous that does this thing, for this deed is evil before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.

cards.note: Genesis 29:17 — *Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.* Jubilees 28:5 expands the same contrast — Leah's eyes weak, Rachel's form handsome — to explain why Jacob loved Rachel more.
cards.s_text: For Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah; for Leah’s eyes were weak, but her form was very handsome; but Rachel had beautiful eyes and a beautiful and very handsome form.
cards.t_text: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.

cards.note: Genesis 29:25 — *And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?* Jubilees 28:4 carries the same dawn-discovery and the same angry charge against Laban.
cards.s_text: And he went in to her, and behold, she was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban, and said to him: “Why have you dealt thus with me? Did not I serve you for Rachel and not for Leah? Why have you wronged me? Take your daughter, and I will go; for you have done evil to me.”
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this you have done unto me? did not I serve with you for Rachel? wherefore then have you beguiled me?

cards.note: Genesis 29:18 — *And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.* The wage Jacob demands in Jubilees 28:2 — “Give me my wife, for whom I have served you seven years” — is the Genesis bargain word for word.
cards.s_text: And in the first year of the third week he said to him: “Give me my wife, for whom I have served you seven years;” and Laban said to Jacob. “I will give you your wife.”
cards.t_text: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.

cards.note: Genesis 29:1 — *Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.* Jubilees 28:1 retells the same arrival at Laban's, adding only that the service for Rachel was “one week” of years.
cards.s_text: And he went on his journey, and came to the land of the east, to Laban, the brother of Rebecca, and he was with him, and served him for Rachel his daughter one week.
cards.t_text: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.

cards.note: Jubilees 27:27 — *...and of all that you give me, I shall give the tenth to you, my Elohim (God).* Earlier Jubilees ties Jacob's vow to the tithe, the same covenant-keeping that closes Jubilees 29:20 in his parents' blessing.
cards.s_text: And thither Jacob sent all that he did send to his father and his mother from time to time, all they needed, and they blessed Jacob with all their heart and with all their soul.
cards.t_text: And Jacob vowed a vow to Yahuah (God), saying: “If Yahuah (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then shall Yahuah (God) be my Elohim (God), and this stone which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, shall be Yahuah (God)’s house, and of all that you give me, I shall give the tenth to you, my Elohim (God).”

cards.note: Genesis 28:22 — *And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be Elohim's (God's) house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.* The tithe-pledge of the Bethel vow stands behind the giving and blessing of Jubilees 29:20.
cards.s_text: And thither Jacob sent all that he did send to his father and his mother from time to time, all they needed, and they blessed Jacob with all their heart and with all their soul.
cards.t_text: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be Elohim's (God’s) house: and of all that you shall give me I will surely give the tenth unto you.

cards.note: Genesis 28:21 — *So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall Yahuah (LORD) be my Elohim (God).* Isaac's return to the tower of Abraham in Jubilees 29:17 is the father's house Jacob vowed to come back to.
cards.s_text: For Isaac had returned from the Well of the Oath and gone up to the tower of his father Abraham, and he dwelt there apart from his son Esau.
cards.t_text: So that I come again to my father’s house in peace; then shall Yahuah (LORD) be my Elohim (God):

cards.note: Genesis 28:20 — *And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If Elohim (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on.* The bread and raiment Jacob asked at Bethel are exactly the food and clothing he sends Isaac in Jubilees 29:15.
cards.s_text: And he sent to his father Isaac of all his substance, clothing, and food, and meat, and drink, and milk, and butter, and cheese, and some dates of the valley,
cards.t_text: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If Elohim (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,

cards.note: Genesis 36:8 — *Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.* The Torah seals Esau's settling in Seir that Jubilees 29:13 marks as his departure.
cards.s_text: And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.
cards.t_text: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.

cards.note: Genesis 33:16 — *So Esau returned that day on his way unto Seir.* Genesis says exactly what Jubilees 29:13 says: Esau departed to the land of Seir.
cards.s_text: And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.
cards.t_text: So Esau returned that day on his way unto Seir.

cards.note: Genesis 33:3 — *And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.* Jacob's bowing approach is the reconciliation Jubilees 29:13 names in a phrase.
cards.s_text: And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.
cards.t_text: And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

cards.note: Genesis 33:1 — *And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids.* Genesis fills out the meeting Jubilees 29:13 records as Esau coming to Jacob.
cards.s_text: And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.
cards.t_text: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids.

cards.note: Amos 2:9 — *Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.* The prophet sings Yahuah's destroying of the towering Amorite that Jubilees 29:11 says replaced the Rephaim.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (God) destroyed them because of the evil of their deeds; for they were very malignant, and the Amorites dwelt in their stead, wicked and sinful, and there is no people to-day which has wrought to the full all their sins, and they have no longer length of life on the earth.
cards.t_text: Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.

cards.note: Joshua 12:4 — *And the coast of Og king of Bashan, which was of the remnant of the giants, that dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei.* Joshua seats the giants at Ashtaroth and Edrei, the very kingdom-seats named in Jubilees 29:10.
cards.s_text: And their habitation was from the land of the children of Ammon to Mount Hermon, and the seats of their kingdom were Karnaim and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, and Mîsûr, and Beon.
cards.t_text: And the coast of Og king of Bashan, which was of the remnant of the giants, that dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,

cards.note: Deuteronomy 3:11 — *For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.* The Torah's last giant-king is exactly the Rephaim Jubilees 29:9-11 says held that land.
cards.s_text: But before they used to call the land of Gilead the land of the Rephaim; for it was the land of the Rephaim, and the Rephaim were born (there), giants whose height was ten, nine, eight down to seven cubits.
cards.t_text: For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.

cards.note: Genesis 31:52 — *This heap be witness, and this pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.* This is the exact non-crossing oath Jubilees 29:7 compresses into a single line.
cards.s_text: And on the fifteenth of those days Jacob made a feast for Laban, and for all who came with him, and Jacob sware to Laban that day, and Laban also to Jacob, that neither should cross the mountain of Gilead to the other with evil purpose.
cards.t_text: This heap be witness, and this pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and that you shall not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.

cards.note: Genesis 31:49 — *And Mizpah; for he said, Yahuah (LORD) watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.* The same heap carries the Mizpah watchword behind Jubilees 29:8's witness.
cards.s_text: And he made there a heap for a witness; wherefore the name of that place is called: “The Heap of Witness,” after this heap.
cards.t_text: And Mizpah; for he said, Yahuah (LORD) watch between me and you, when we are absent one from another.

cards.note: Genesis 31:48 — *And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed.* The 'Heap of Witness' Jubilees 29:8 names is Genesis' Galeed.
cards.s_text: And he made there a heap for a witness; wherefore the name of that place is called: “The Heap of Witness,” after this heap.
cards.t_text: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and you this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed;

cards.note: Genesis 31:44 — *Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee.* Laban's proposal is the covenant-oath Jubilees 29:7 says the two men swore.
cards.s_text: And on the fifteenth of those days Jacob made a feast for Laban, and for all who came with him, and Jacob sware to Laban that day, and Laban also to Jacob, that neither should cross the mountain of Gilead to the other with evil purpose.
cards.t_text: Now therefore come you, let us make a covenant, I and you; and let it be for a witness between me and you.

cards.note: *And Jacob vowed a vow to Yahuah (God), saying: “If Yahuah (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then shall Yahuah (God) be my Elohim (God), and this stone which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, shall be Yahuah (God)’s house, and of all that you give me, I shall give the tenth to you, my Elohim (God).”* (Jubilees 27:27). *For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, even all that He had spoken to him that he should return to his father’s house; and they said: “To every place whither you go we will go with you.”* (Jubilees 29:3). Jacob's vow at Bethel asks for one thing in particular: to come again to his father's house in peace. Years later, when he tells his wives why they are leaving Laban, what he tells them is a dream in which Yahuah (God) spoke to him that he should return to his father's house. The vow and the dream use the same words because the dream is the answer to the vow. Jubilees lets the reader see both ends of it: the stone set up as a pillar with a promise attached, and the command that sends him back to keep it.
cards.s_text: For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, even all that He had spoken to him that he should return to his father’s house; and they said: “To every place whither you go we will go with you.”
cards.t_text: And Jacob vowed a vow to Yahuah (God), saying: “If Yahuah (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then shall Yahuah (God) be my Elohim (God), and this stone which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, shall be Yahuah (God)’s house, and of all that you give me, I shall give the tenth to you, my Elohim (God).”

cards.note: Genesis 31:3 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.* The dream Jubilees 29:3 reports is Yahuah's spoken command to return home.
cards.s_text: For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, even all that He had spoken to him that he should return to his father’s house; and they said: “To every place whither you go we will go with you.”
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of your fathers, and to your kindred; and I will be with you.

cards.note: Genesis 31:4 — *And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock.* Genesis records the very summons Jubilees 29:2 retells, Jacob calling Leah and Rachel to him.
cards.s_text: And Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and spake kindly to them that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.
cards.t_text: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock,

cards.note: Genesis 31:2 — *And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and, behold, it was not toward him as before.* The turn in Laban's face is the same cause Jubilees gives for Jacob calling his wives to leave.
cards.s_text: And Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and spake kindly to them that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.
cards.t_text: And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and, behold, it was not toward him as before.

cards.note: Revelation 3:5 — *He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.* The Messiah keeps the same book of life Jubilees 30:22 says the unfaithful are blotted from.
cards.s_text: But if they transgress and work uncleanness in every way, they will be recorded on the heavenly tables as adversaries, and they will be destroyed out of the book of life, and they will be recorded in the book of those who will be destroyed and with those who will be rooted out of the earth.
cards.t_text: He that overcomes, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.

cards.note: Malachi 3:16 — *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* The favourable inscription on the heavenly tables in Jubilees 30:19 is Malachi's book of remembrance for the faithful.
cards.s_text: And so they inscribe as a testimony in his favour on the heavenly tables blessing and righteousness before the Elohim (God) of all:
cards.t_text: Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.

cards.note: Psalm 69:28 — *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.* The book of the living and the writing of the righteous are the two columns of the heavenly tables in Jubilees 30:21.
cards.s_text: All this account I have written for you, and have commanded you to say to the children of Yashar’el (Israel), that they should not commit sin nor transgress the ordinances nor break the covenant which has been ordained for them, (but) that they should fulfil it and be recorded as friends.
cards.t_text: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.

cards.note: Exodus 32:33 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.* The blotting from the book is exactly the destruction out of the book of life threatened in Jubilees 30:22.
cards.s_text: But if they transgress and work uncleanness in every way, they will be recorded on the heavenly tables as adversaries, and they will be destroyed out of the book of life, and they will be recorded in the book of those who will be destroyed and with those who will be rooted out of the earth.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Whosoever has sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.

cards.note: Exodus 32:32 — *Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.* Moses' plea names the very book that Jubilees 30:19-21 calls the heavenly tables — the register of blessing and destruction.
cards.s_text: And so they inscribe as a testimony in his favour on the heavenly tables blessing and righteousness before the Elohim (God) of all:
cards.t_text: Yet now, if you will forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray you, out of your book which you have written.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 33:9 — *Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant.* Levi's setting of covenant above kin is the same zeal reckoned for righteousness in Jubilees 30:17,18.
cards.s_text: For this reason I have commanded you, saying: "Testify this testimony to Yashar’el (Israel): see how the Shechemites fared and their sons: how they were delivered into the hands of two sons of Jacob, and they slew them under tortures, and it was (reckoned) to them for righteousness, and it is written down to them for righteousness.
cards.t_text: Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed your word, and kept your covenant.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 33:10 — *They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.* Moses' blessing seals the priestly ministry Jubilees 30:18 says Levi was chosen for — to minister before Yahuah continually.
cards.s_text: And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before Yahuah (God), as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Yashar’el (Israel).
cards.t_text: They shall teach Jacob your judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) your law: they shall put incense before you, and whole burnt sacrifice upon your altar.

cards.note: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The everlasting priesthood given for zeal is precisely the blessing Jubilees 30:18 lays on Levi and his sons.
cards.s_text: And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before Yahuah (God), as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Yashar’el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Numbers 25:11 — *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* The zeal-counted-righteous that wins Levi the priesthood in Jubilees 30:18 is the same zeal of Phinehas, a Levite.
cards.s_text: And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before Yahuah (God), as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Yashar’el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.

cards.note: Malachi 2:11 — *Yahudah (Judah) hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Yashar'el (Israel) and in Jerusalem; for Yahudah (Judah) hath profaned the holiness of Yahuah (LORD) which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.* Malachi names the profaning of holiness Jubilees 30:15 foretells when Israel marries the daughters of the nations.
cards.s_text: For there will be plague upon plague, and curse upon curse, and every judgment and plague and curse will come (upon him): if he do this thing, or hide his eyes from those who commit uncleanness, or those who defile the sanctuary of Yahuah (God), or those who profane His holy name, (then) will the whole nation together be judged for all the uncleanness and profanation of this (man).
cards.t_text: Yahudah (Judah) has dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Yashar'el (Israel) and in Jerusalem; for Yahudah (Judah) has profaned the holiness of Yahuah (LORD) which he loved, and has married the daughter of a strange god.

cards.note: Ezra 10:11 — *Now therefore make confession unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of your fathers, and do his pleasure: and separate yourselves from the people of the land, and from the strange wives.* The separation Ezra commands is the remedy for the very profanation Jubilees 30:15 warns will bring curse upon the nation.
cards.s_text: For there will be plague upon plague, and curse upon curse, and every judgment and plague and curse will come (upon him): if he do this thing, or hide his eyes from those who commit uncleanness, or those who defile the sanctuary of Yahuah (God), or those who profane His holy name, (then) will the whole nation together be judged for all the uncleanness and profanation of this (man).
cards.t_text: Now therefore make confession unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of your fathers, and do his pleasure: and separate yourselves from the people of the land, and from the strange wives.

cards.note: Ezra 9:12 — *Now therefore give not your daughters unto their sons, neither take their daughters unto your sons, nor seek their peace or their wealth for ever: that ye may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children for ever.* Ezra repeats the give-not/take-not statute of Jubilees 30:11,14 verbatim in form.
cards.s_text: And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Now therefore give not your daughters unto their sons, neither take their daughters unto your sons, nor seek their peace or their wealth for ever: that you may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children for ever.

cards.note: Ezra 9:2 — *For they have taken of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands: yea, the hand of the princes and rulers hath been chief in this trespass.* The mingled holy seed Ezra mourns is exactly the uncleanness Jubilees 30:14 forbids.
cards.s_text: And Yashar’el (Israel) will not be free from this uncleanness if it has a wife of the daughters of the nations, or has given any of its daughters to a man who is of any of the nations.
cards.t_text: For they have taken of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands: yea, the hand of the princes and rulers has been chief in this trespass.

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 6:14 — *Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?* The apostle carries the same uncleanness-separation of Jubilees 30:14 forward into the assembly.
cards.s_text: And Yashar’el (Israel) will not be free from this uncleanness if it has a wife of the daughters of the nations, or has given any of its daughters to a man who is of any of the nations.
cards.t_text: Be you not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship has righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion has light with darkness?

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:6 — *For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* The holiness Jubilees 30:8 invokes — Israel holy to Yahuah — is election, the ground of the separation.
cards.s_text: And let not an adulteress and no uncleanness be found in Yashar’el (Israel) throughout all the days of the generations of the earth; for Yashar’el (Israel) is holy to Yahuah (God), and every man who has defiled (it) shall surely die: they shall stone him with stones.
cards.t_text: For you are an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has chosen you to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 24:3 — *And I will make thee swear by Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, and the Elohim (God) of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell.* Abraham's oath shows the seed-kept-separate law standing in Genesis itself, long before Jubilees 30:11.
cards.s_text: And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And I will make you swear by Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, and the Elohim (God) of the earth, that you shall not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:4 — *For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of Yahuah (LORD) be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.* This gives Jubilees 30's reason: the seed is kept separate to keep the heart from turning to other gods, not for race.
cards.s_text: And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: For they will turn away your son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of Yahuah (LORD) be kindled against you, and destroy you suddenly.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:3 — *Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.* The very command Jubilees 30:11 puts in Moses' mouth, word for word the Torah's marriage law.
cards.s_text: And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Neither shall you make marriages with them; your daughter you shall not give unto his son, nor his daughter shall you take unto your son.

cards.note: Genesis 34:27 — *The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city, because they had defiled their sister.* The spoiling of Shechem and the rescue of Dinah in Jubilees 30:24 follow Genesis exactly.
cards.s_text: And they brought Dinah, their sister, out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive everything that was in Shechem, their sheep and their oxen and their asses, and all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought them all to Jacob their father.
cards.t_text: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city, because they had defiled their sister.

cards.note: Genesis 34:25 — *And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* The two avengers of Jubilees 30:4 are named in Genesis as Simeon and Levi.
cards.s_text: And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and slew all the men whom they found in it, and left not a single one remaining in it: they slew all in torments because they had dishonoured their sister Dinah.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.

cards.note: Genesis 34:7 — *And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.* The wrath of Jacob and his sons in Jubilees 30:3 is the wrath Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And he besought his father and her brothers that she might be given to him to wife. And Jacob and his sons were wroth because of the men of Shechem; for they had defiled Dinah, their sister, and they spake to them with evil intent and dealt deceitfully with them and beguiled them.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.

cards.note: Genesis 34:2 — *And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.* The Genesis source for Jubilees 30:2, naming the same prince and the same defiling of Dinah.
cards.s_text: And there they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite, the prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her, and she was a little girl, a child of twelve years.
cards.t_text: And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.

cards.note: Malachi 3:16 — *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* The eternal testimony inscribed for Levi and Judah (Jubilees 31:32) is this book of remembrance written before Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And he said: “Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons also, before the Elohim (God) of all;” and thus is it ordained concerning the two; and they record it as an eternal testimony to them on the heavenly tables how Isaac blessed them.
cards.t_text: Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.

cards.note: *And he said: “Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons also, before the Elohim (God) of all;” and thus is it ordained concerning the two; and they record it as an eternal testimony to them on the heavenly tables how Isaac blessed them.* (Jubilees 31:32). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). Isaac's blessing on Levi and Judah is not left to the wind; it is recorded on the heavenly tables as an eternal testimony. David looked into that same book and found his own members written there before any of them were. The book holds both: a man's frame before he is formed, and a father's blessing after it is spoken. Isaac can say "now I know that I have an eternal hope" because what is written in heaven does not fade with the voice that spoke it.
cards.s_text: And he said: “Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons also, before the Elohim (God) of all;” and thus is it ordained concerning the two; and they record it as an eternal testimony to them on the heavenly tables how Isaac blessed them.
cards.t_text: Your eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in your book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.

cards.note: Genesis 27:29 — *Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee… cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.* Isaac repeats over Levi and Judah (Jubilees 31:17) the same seal he once spoke over Jacob himself.
cards.s_text: And let all who hate you fall down before you, And let all your adversaries be rooted out and perish; And blessed be he that blesses you, And cursed be every nation that curses you.
cards.t_text: Let people serve you, and nations bow down to you: be lord over your brethren, and let your mother’s sons bow down to you: cursed be every one that curses you, and blessed be he that blesses you.

cards.note: Genesis 12:3 — *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.* Isaac's blessed-be-he-that-blesses-you / cursed-be-the-nation-that-curses-you (Jubilees 31:17) is the Abrahamic promise carried onto Levi.
cards.s_text: And let all who hate you fall down before you, And let all your adversaries be rooted out and perish; And blessed be he that blesses you, And cursed be every nation that curses you.
cards.t_text: And I will bless them that bless you, and curse him that curses you: and in you shall all families of the earth be blessed.

cards.note: Revelation 5:5 — *And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.* The throne of righteousness Judah sits on (Jubilees 31:20) is the throne of the Lion of Judah who prevails.
cards.s_text: And when you sit on the throne of the honour of your righteousness, There will be great peace for all the seed of the sons of the beloved, And blessed will he be that blesses you; And all that hate you and afflict you and curse you Shall be rooted out and destroyed from the earth and accursed."
cards.t_text: And one of the elders says unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.

cards.note: Hebrews 7:14 — *For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* The deliverer found in Judah (Jubilees 31:19) is the Lord the New Testament says sprang out of Judah.
cards.s_text: In you shall be the help of Jacob, And in you be found the salvation of Yashar’el (Israel).
cards.t_text: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.

cards.note: Numbers 24:17 — *I shall see him, but not now… there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.* The salvation of Israel in Judah (Jubilees 31:19) is the Sceptre that rises out of Israel.
cards.s_text: In you shall be the help of Jacob, And in you be found the salvation of Yashar’el (Israel).
cards.t_text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.

cards.note: Genesis 49:8 — *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.* Treading down all that hate him and ruling the sons of Jacob (Jubilees 31:18) echoes Judah's hand on the enemy's neck.
cards.s_text: And to Yahudah (Judah) he said: May Yahuah (God) give you strength and power To tread down all that hate you; A prince shall you be, you and one of your sons, over the sons of Jacob; May your name and the name of your sons go forth and traverse every land and region. Then will the nations fear before your face, And all the nations will quake And all the peoples will quake.
cards.t_text: Yahudah (Judah), you are he whom your brethren shall praise: your hand shall be in the neck of your enemies; your father’s children shall bow down before you.

cards.note: Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* The prince-over-the-sons-of-Jacob blessing of Jubilees 31:18 is Jacob's undeparting sceptre of Judah.
cards.s_text: And to Yahudah (Judah) he said: May Yahuah (God) give you strength and power To tread down all that hate you; A prince shall you be, you and one of your sons, over the sons of Jacob; May your name and the name of your sons go forth and traverse every land and region. Then will the nations fear before your face, And all the nations will quake And all the peoples will quake.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: Malachi 2:7 — *For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* The mouth that speaks Yahuah's word in righteousness (Jubilees 31:15) is the covenant of Levi the prophet still holds Levi to.
cards.s_text: And they will be princes and judges, and chiefs of all the seed of the sons of Jacob; They will speak the word of Yahuah (God) in righteousness, And they will judge all His judgments in righteousness. And they will declare My ways to Jacob And My paths to Yashar’el (Israel). The blessing of Yahuah (God) will be given in their mouths To bless all the seed of the beloved.
cards.t_text: For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).

cards.note: Numbers 18:2 — *And thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi, the tribe of thy father, bring thou with thee, that they may be joined unto thee, and minister unto thee: but thou and thy sons with thee shall minister before the tabernacle of witness.* The Levites' joining to minister is the drawing-near to serve Isaac foretells in Jubilees 31:14.
cards.s_text: And may Yahuah (God) give to you and to your seed greatness and great glory, and cause you and your seed, from among all flesh, to approach Him to serve in His sanctuary as the angels of the presence and as the holy ones. (Even) as they, will the seed of your sons be for glory and greatness and holiness, and may He make them great to all the ages.
cards.t_text: And your brethren also of the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, bring you with you, that they may be joined unto you, and minister unto you: but you and your sons with you shall minister before the tabernacle of witness.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 10:8 — *At that time Yahuah (LORD) separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD), to stand before Yahuah (LORD) to minister unto him, and to bless in his name, unto this day.* Levi's seed approaching to serve in the sanctuary (Jubilees 31:14) is the separated tribe that stands before Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And may Yahuah (God) give to you and to your seed greatness and great glory, and cause you and your seed, from among all flesh, to approach Him to serve in His sanctuary as the angels of the presence and as the holy ones. (Even) as they, will the seed of your sons be for glory and greatness and holiness, and may He make them great to all the ages.
cards.t_text: At that time Yahuah (LORD) separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD), to stand before Yahuah (LORD) to minister unto him, and to bless in his name, unto this day.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 33:10 — *They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.* Levi declaring Yahuah's ways to Jacob and His paths to Israel (Jubilees 31:15) is this same teaching office.
cards.s_text: And they will be princes and judges, and chiefs of all the seed of the sons of Jacob; They will speak the word of Yahuah (God) in righteousness, And they will judge all His judgments in righteousness. And they will declare My ways to Jacob And My paths to Yashar’el (Israel). The blessing of Yahuah (God) will be given in their mouths To bless all the seed of the beloved.
cards.t_text: They shall teach Jacob your judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) your law: they shall put incense before you, and whole burnt sacrifice upon your altar.
