cards.s_text: And Cain hastened and rose up, and took the iron part of his ploughing instrument, with which he suddenly smote his brother and he slew him, and Cain spilt the blood of his brother Abel upon the earth, and the blood of Abel streamed upon the earth before the flock.
cards.t_text: And he slew him in the field: and his blood cried from the ground to heaven, complaining because he had slain him.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:4 — *And Yahuah (God) reproved Cain because of Abel, because he had slain him, and he made him a fugitive on the earth because of the blood of his brother, and he cursed him upon the earth...* Jubilees gives the same curse and fugitive-sentence Jasher 1:31 records — the now-live witness, adding the heavenly-tables verdict on treacherous murder.
cards.s_text: But you did this thing and did slay your brother for naught and because he spoke rightly to you, and now, therefore, cursed be you from the ground which opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand, and wherein you did bury him.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) reproved Cain because of Abel, because he had slain him, and he made him a fugitive on the earth because of the blood of his brother, and he cursed him upon the earth.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:31 — *At the close of this jubilee Cain was killed after him in the same year; for his house fell upon him and he died in the midst of his house, and he was killed by its stones, for with a stone he had killed Abel, and by a stone was he killed in righteous judgment.* Jubilees follows the same Cain whose city Jasher 1:35 builds to his stone-struck end in righteous judgment — the now-live witness.
cards.s_text: And at that time Cain also began to build a city: and he built the city and he called the name of the city Enoch, according to the name of his son; for in those days Yahuah (the Lord) had given him rest upon the earth, and he did not move about and wander as in the beginning.
cards.t_text: At the close of this jubilee Cain was killed after him in the same year; for his house fell upon him and he died in the midst of his house, and he was killed by its stones, for with a stone he had killed Abel, and by a stone was he killed in righteous judgment.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:15 — *Mahalalel took to him to wife Dînâh, the daughter of Barâkî'êl the daughter of his father's brother, and she bare him a son... and he called his name Jared; for in his days the angels of Yahuah (God) descended on the earth, those who are named the Watchers, that they should instruct the children of men.* Jubilees carries the same Mahalaleel-Jared generation of Jasher 2:37 and marks Jared's days as when the Watchers came down — the corruption Jasher's next chapters and 1 Enoch unfold.
cards.s_text: And Mahlallel the son of Cainan lived sixty-five years and he begat Jared; and Jared lived sixty-two years and he begat Enoch.
cards.t_text: And in the second week of the tenth jubilee Mahalalel took to him to wife Dînâh, the daughter of Barâkî’êl the daughter of his father’s brother, and she bare him a son in the third week in the sixth year, and he called his name Jared; for in his days the angels of Yahuah (God) descended on the earth, those who are named the Watchers, that they should instruct the children of men, and that they should do judgment and uprightness on the earth.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:31 — *Cain was killed after him in the same year; for his house fell upon him and he died in the midst of his house, and he was killed by its stones, for with a stone he had killed Abel, and by a stone was he killed in righteous judgment.* Both Jasher 2:29 and Jubilees end Cain in measure-for-measure judgment for Abel's blood — the same event, both now live.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) requited Cain’s evil according to his wickedness, which he had done to his brother Abel, according to the word of Yahuah (the Lord) which he had spoken.
cards.t_text: At the close of this jubilee Cain was killed after him in the same year; for his house fell upon him and he died in the midst of his house, and he was killed by its stones, for with a stone he had killed Abel, and by a stone was he killed in righteous judgment.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:17 — *And he was the first among men that are born on earth who learnt writing and knowledge and wisdom and who wrote down the signs of heaven according to the order of their months in a book, that men might know the seasons of the years according to the order of their separate months.* Cainan's writing of things to come on stone tablets in Jasher 2:13 mirrors the chosen line's scribal foreknowledge that Jubilees gives to Enoch.
cards.s_text: And in those days Cainan wrote upon tablets of stone, what was to take place in time to come, and he put them in his treasures.
cards.t_text: And he was the first among men that are born on earth who learnt writing and knowledge and wisdom and who wrote down the signs of heaven according to the order of their months in a book, that men might know the seasons of the years according to the order of their separate months.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:7 — *Adam knew his wife again, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said "Elohim (God) has raised up a second seed to us on the earth instead of Abel; for Cain slew him."* Jubilees narrates the identical appointed-seed scene of Jasher 2:1 — both now live, the same election.
cards.s_text: And it was in the hundred and thirtieth year of the life of Adam upon the earth, that he again knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bare a son in his likeness and in his image, and she called his name Seth, saying, Because Elohim (God) has appointed me another seed in the place of Abel, for Cain has slain him.
cards.t_text: And Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years, and in the fourth year of the fifth week they became joyful, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said “Elohim (God) has raised up a second seed to us on the earth instead of Abel; for Cain slew him.”

cards.note: Jubilees 4:16 — *And in the eleventh jubilee Jared took to himself a wife... and she bare him a son in the fifth week, in the fourth year of the jubilee, and he called his name Enoch.* the same patriarchal birth Jasher 3:1 records, both tracing the seed-line generation by generation.
cards.s_text: And Enoch lived sixty-five years and he begat Methuselah; and Enoch walked with Elohim (God) after having begot Methuselah, and he served Yahuah (the Lord), and despised the evil ways of men.
cards.t_text: And in the eleventh jubilee Jared took to himself a wife, and her name was Bâraka, the daughter of Râsûjâl, a daughter of his father’s brother, in the fourth week of this jubilee, and she bare him a son in the fifth week, in the fourth year of the jubilee, and he called his name Enoch.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:17–18 — *And he was the first among men that are born on earth who learnt writing and knowledge and wisdom... And he was the first to write a testimony, and he testified to the sons of men among the generations of the earth* the wisdom Jasher 3:8 says the spirit of Elohim gave Enoch to teach all his men.
cards.s_text: And the spirit of Elohim was upon Enoch, and he taught all his men the wisdom of Elohim and his ways, and the sons of Adam served Yahuah (the Lord) all the days of Enoch, and they came to hear his wisdom.
cards.t_text: And he was the first among men that are born on earth who learnt writing and knowledge and wisdom and who wrote down the signs of heaven according to the order of their months in a book, that men might know the seasons of the years according to the order of their separate months.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:30 — *And he lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens and therefore was it written concerning the tree of knowledge: "On the day that you eat thereof you will die."* the very tree-of-knowledge death Jasher 3:16 names as the cause of Adam's dying.
cards.s_text: And Adam died because he ate of the tree of knowledge; he and his children after him, as Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) had spoken.
cards.t_text: And he lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens and therefore was it written concerning the tree of knowledge: “On the day that you eat thereof you will die.” For this reason he did not complete the years of this day; for he died during it.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:29 — *And at the close of the nineteenth jubilee... Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.* the burial Jasher 3:14 records with Enoch and Methuselah laying Adam in the cave with great pomp.
cards.s_text: And it was in the fifty-sixth year of the life of Lamech when Adam died; nine hundred and thirty years old was he at his death, and his two sons, with Enoch and Methuselah his son, buried him with great pomp, as at the burial of kings, in the cave which Elohim had told him.
cards.t_text: And at the close of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week in the sixth year thereof, Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:23 — *And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour, and behold there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world* the taking-up Jasher 3:23 sets in motion when the angel calls Enoch to reign in heaven.
cards.s_text: And in some time after, when the kings and princes and the sons of men were speaking to Enoch, and Enoch was teaching them the ways of Elohim, behold an angel of Yahuah (the Lord) then called to Enoch from heaven, and wished to bring him up to heaven to make him reign there over the sons of Elohim, as he had reigned over the sons of men upon earth.
cards.t_text: And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour, and behold there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:19 — *And what was and what will be he saw in a vision of his sleep... he saw and understood everything, and wrote his testimony, and placed the testimony on earth for all the children of men and for their generations.* the parting wisdom Jasher 3:25 has Enoch leave so the sons of men may live.
cards.s_text: And now therefore I will teach you wisdom and knowledge and will give you instruction before I leave you, how to act upon earth by which you may live; and he did so.
cards.t_text: And what was and what will be he saw in a vision of his sleep, as it will happen to the children of men throughout their generations until the day of judgment; he saw and understood everything, and wrote his testimony, and placed the testimony on earth for all the children of men and for their generations.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:24 — *he was set as a sign and that he should testify against all the children of men, that he should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.* the witness-to-the-generations role behind Jasher 3:31, where Enoch's last day teaching bids all men serve Yahuah and walk in his ways.
cards.s_text: And all the sons of Adam assembled and came to Enoch that day; and all the kings of the earth with their princes and counsellors remained with him that day; and Enoch then taught the sons of men wisdom and knowledge, and gave them divine instruction; and he bade them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways all the days of their lives, and he continued to make peace amongst them.
cards.t_text: And on account of it Elohim (God) brought the waters of the flood upon all the land of Eden; for there he was set as a sign and that he should testify against all the children of men, that he should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.

cards.note: Jubilees 5:5 — *But Noah found grace before the eyes of Yahuah (God).* The same election of Noah out of the doomed world that Jasher 4:21 declares.
cards.s_text: And Noah found grace in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and Yahuah (the Lord) chose him and his children to raise up seed from them upon the face of the whole earth.
cards.t_text: But Noah found grace before the eyes of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: Jubilees 5:2 — *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth...* the same mixture of all flesh, men and animals, that Jasher 4:18 says corrupted its ways upon earth.
cards.s_text: And their judges and rulers went to the daughters of men and took their wives by force from their husbands according to their choice, and the sons of men in those days took from the cattle of the earth, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air, and taught the mixture of animals of one species with the other, in order therewith to provoke Yahuah (the Lord); and Elohim saw the whole earth and it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its ways upon earth, all men and all animals.
cards.t_text: And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth-all of them corrupted their ways and their orders, and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth and every imagination of the thoughts of all men (was) thus evil continually.

cards.note: Jubilees 5:19 — *...no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons... for his heart was righteous in all his ways...* the same righteous Noah Jasher 4:15 says walked perfect and upright with Elohim while all flesh corrupted.
cards.s_text: And the child grew up and was weaned, and he went in the ways of his father Methuselah, perfect and upright with Elohim.
cards.t_text: And as for all those who corrupted their ways and their thoughts before the flood, no man’s person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways, according as it was commanded regarding him, and he had not departed from aught that was ordained for him.

cards.note: Jubilees 5:19 — *And as for all those who corrupted their ways and their thoughts before the flood, no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account...* The fathers who followed Yahuah die out (Jasher 5:5), leaving Noah alone as the accepted remnant.
cards.s_text: And all who followed Yahuah (the Lord) died in those days, before they saw the evil which Elohim (God) declared to do upon earth.
cards.t_text: And as for all those who corrupted their ways and their thoughts before the flood, no man’s person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways, according as it was commanded regarding him, and he had not departed from aught that was ordained for him.

cards.note: *And He said “Your spirit will not always abide on man; for they also are flesh and their days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”* (Jubilees 5:8). *For thus says Yahuah (the Lord), Behold I give you a period of one hundred and twenty years; if you will turn to me and forsake your evil ways, then will I also turn away from the evil which I told you, and it shall not exist, says Yahuah (the Lord).* (Jasher 5:8). Both books put the same number on the same mercy. In Jubilees it is a limit set on flesh: the Spirit will not always abide on man, and a hundred and twenty years is the measure. Jasher hears it as a door left open: a period of a hundred and twenty years, and if you will turn to me the evil will not come. Genesis 6:3 carries the number; these two tell you it was a space for repentance before the flood, not merely a lifespan. The decree and the offer were the same hundred and twenty years.
cards.s_text: For thus says Yahuah (the Lord), Behold I give you a period of one hundred and twenty years; if you will turn to me and forsake your evil ways, then will I also turn away from the evil which I told you, and it shall not exist, says Yahuah (the Lord).
cards.t_text: And He said “Your spirit will not always abide on man; for they also are flesh and their days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”

cards.note: *And Noah made the ark in all respects as He commanded him, in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, in the fifth week in the fifth year (on the new moon of the first month).* (Jubilees 5:22). *And Noah rose up, and he made the ark, in the place where Elohim had commanded him, and Noah did as Elohim had ordered him.* (Jasher 5:33). Jasher says Noah rose up and made the ark where Elohim (God) commanded; Jubilees says he made it in all respects as He commanded, and gives the date. Obedience is the point in both. Jubilees adds the calendar, the twenty-seventh jubilee, fifth week, fifth year, on the new moon of the first month, because Jubilees counts everything by the reckoning of time Yahuah (God) gave. The ark was built on command, in the right place, and on a dated day.
cards.s_text: And Noah rose up, and he made the ark, in the place where Elohim had commanded him, and Noah did as Elohim had ordered him.
cards.t_text: And Noah made the ark in all respects as He commanded him, in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, in the fifth week in the fifth year (on the new moon of the first month).

cards.note: Jubilees 5:23 — *he entered, and all that we brought to him, into the ark, and Yahuah (God) closed it from without on the seventeenth evening.* Jubilees keeps the same record of the creatures brought in that Jasher 6:8 narrates, both witnesses now live.
cards.s_text: And Noah brought into the ark from all living creatures that were upon earth, so that there was none left but which Noah brought into the ark.
cards.t_text: And he entered in the sixth (year) thereof, in the second month, on the new moon of the second month, till the sixteenth; and he entered, and all that we brought to him, into the ark, and Yahuah (God) closed it from without on the seventeenth evening.

cards.note: Jubilees 5:24 — *And Yahuah (God) opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.* Jubilees keeps the same fountains-of-the-deep that Jasher 6:14 reports, the patriarchal record self-linked.
cards.s_text: And all the fountains of the deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened, and the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.

cards.note: Jubilees 5:19 — *no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways.* Jubilees names the same righteous remnant shut into the ark of Jasher 6:15, the election of the seed-line kept.
cards.s_text: And Noah and his household, and all the living creatures that were with him, came into the ark on account of the waters of the flood, and Yahuah (the Lord) shut him in.
cards.t_text: And as for all those who corrupted their ways and their thoughts before the flood, no man’s person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways, according as it was commanded regarding him, and he had not departed from aught that was ordained for him.

cards.note: Jubilees 6:5 — *And you, increase you and multiply upon the earth, and become many upon it, and be a blessing upon it.* Jubilees keeps the same multiply-and-be-a-blessing word that Jasher 6:42 carries, the patriarchal record self-linked.
cards.s_text: And he said to them, Be fruitful and fill all the earth; become strong and increase abundantly in the earth and multiply in it.
cards.t_text: "And you, increase you and multiply upon the earth, and become many upon it, and be a blessing upon it. The fear of you and the dread of you I shall inspire in everything that is on earth and in the sea.

cards.note: Jubilees 6:4 — *And Yahuah (God) smelt the goodly savour, and He made a covenant with him that there should not be any more a flood to destroy the earth.* Jubilees keeps the same altar-savour and no-more-flood covenant that follows the service of Jasher 6:41.
cards.s_text: And they went and returned every one to his way and to his place, and Noah and his sons dwelt in the land that Elohim had told them, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons on their going out from the ark.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) smelt the goodly savour, and He made a covenant with him that there should not be any more a flood to destroy the earth; that all the days of the earth seed-time and harvest should never cease; cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night should not change their order, nor cease for ever.

cards.note: Jubilees 6:16 — *He set His bow in the cloud for a sign of the eternal covenant that there should not again be a flood on the earth to destroy it all the days of the earth.* Jubilees keeps the bow of the eternal covenant that crowns Noah's going-forth in Jasher 6:41, self-linked.
cards.s_text: And they went and returned every one to his way and to his place, and Noah and his sons dwelt in the land that Elohim had told them, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons on their going out from the ark.
cards.t_text: He set His bow in the cloud for a sign of the eternal covenant that there should not again be a flood on the earth to destroy it all the days of the earth.

cards.note: *And it came to pass in the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem and Ham and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year in the first week, when one of us, who had been sent, was with them.* (Jubilees 8:10). *And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.* (Jasher 7:1). Jasher names the three sons and says children were born to them after the flood; Jubilees picks up once those families have grown and shows the earth divided into three parts, one for each son, by inheritance. The division was not a scramble for land; one who had been sent, an angel, was present with them as they did it. The brothers of Jasher 7 become the heads of the three portions of the whole earth. What Jasher begins as a family list, Jubilees finishes as a map.
cards.s_text: And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem and Ham and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year in the first week, when one of us, who had been sent, was with them.

cards.note: *And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.* (Jubilees 8:8). *These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.* (Jasher 7:19). Both books explain the name the same way: Peleg means division, and he was named for what was happening in his days. Jasher says the sons of men were divided and in the latter days the earth was divided; Jubilees says the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves when he was born. The name is a date stamp. Eber named his son after a world event, and both books kept the reason.
cards.s_text: These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.

cards.note: *For they departed from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar; for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Go to, let us ascend thereby into heaven.”* (Jubilees 10:19). *And whilst he was reigning according to his heart’s desire, after having conquered all his enemies around, he advised with his counselors to build a city for his palace, and they did so.* (Jasher 7:42). Jasher gives the man: Nimrod, reigning after his heart's desire, advised by his counselors to build a city for his palace. Jubilees gives the place and the boast: they left Ararat eastward to Shinar and built the city and the tower to climb into heaven by it. Put together, the tower was a king's project with a king's ambition, not a village's. "In his days" in Jubilees is Nimrod's days, and Jasher tells you who he was.
cards.s_text: And whilst he was reigning according to his heart’s desire, after having conquered all his enemies around, he advised with his counselors to build a city for his palace, and they did so.
cards.t_text: For they departed from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar; for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Go to, let us ascend thereby into heaven.”

cards.note: Jubilees 12:7 — *And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.* Terah's fear of the people matches Jasher's Terah trembling before Nimrod's threat over his household.
cards.s_text: And the king hearkened to Terah, and he did so and he gave him three days’ time, and Terah went out from the king’s presence, and he came home to his family and spoke to them all the words of the king; and the people were greatly afraid.
cards.t_text: And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.”

cards.note: Jubilees 12:4–5 — *Worship the Elohim (God) of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth, And does everything upon the earth... Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them?* Jubilees gives the same father — an idolater Abram must rebuke — that Jasher shows bargaining with Nimrod.
cards.s_text: And Terah saw that the anger of the king was kindled against him, and he answered the king, saying, All that I have is in the king’s power; whatever the king desires to do to his servant, that let him do, yea, even my son, he is in the king’s power, without value in exchange, he and his two brothers that are older than he.
cards.t_text: Worship the Elohim (God) of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth, And does everything upon the earth, And has created everything by His word, And all life is from before His face.

cards.note: Jubilees 11:2 — *And the sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all (began) to do evil.* The Jubilees portrait of the kingdoms-of-man rising in Nimrod's generation — the very throne menacing Abram's house.
cards.s_text: And it was in the third day that the king sent to Terah, saying, Send me your son for a price as I spoke to you; and should you not do this, I will send and slay all you have in your house, so that you shall not even have a dog remaining.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all (began) to do evil, and to acquire arms, and to teach their sons war, and they began to capture cities, and to sell male and female slaves.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:16 — *And in the sixth week, in the fifth year thereof, Abram sat up throughout the night on the new moon of the seventh month to observe the stars from the evening to the morning, in order to see what would be the character of the year with regard to the rains, and he was alone as he sat and observed.* The same star-watching Chaldean world that frames Abram's birth in Jasher; Jubilees has Abram himself reading the heavens.
cards.s_text: And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth week, in the fifth year thereof, Abram sat up throughout the night on the new moon of the seventh month to observe the stars from the evening to the morning, in order to see what would be the character of the year with regard to the rains, and he was alone as he sat and observed.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:17 — *All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search (them) out?* Jubilees records the same reasoning — Abram turning from the host of heaven to the One in whose hand they are (Jasher 9:19).
cards.s_text: And Abram said to himself Surely these are not gods that made the earth and all mankind, but these are the servants of Elohim, and Abram remained in the house of Noah and there knew Yahuah (the Lord) and his ways’ and he served Yahuah (the Lord) all the days of his life, and all that generation forgot Yahuah (the Lord), and served other gods of wood and stone, and rebelled all their days.
cards.t_text: And a word came into his heart and he said: "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search (them) out?

cards.note: *And for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it ascends and skirts the river.* (Jubilees 9:3). *And Ashur son of Shem and his children and household went forth at that time, a very large body of them, and they went to a distant land that they found, and they met with a very extensive valley in the land that they went to, and they built themselves four cities, and they called them after their own names and occurrences.* (Jasher 10:32). Jasher tells of Asshur son of Shem going out with a large company to a distant land, finding a wide valley, and building four cities named after themselves. Jubilees had already allotted him that ground: the second portion of Shem's share, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar to the border of India. Jasher's "distant land that they found" was not stumbled upon; it was his by lot. The walking and the allotment are the same inheritance seen from two sides.
cards.s_text: And Ashur son of Shem and his children and household went forth at that time, a very large body of them, and they went to a distant land that they found, and they met with a very extensive valley in the land that they went to, and they built themselves four cities, and they called them after their own names and occurrences.
cards.t_text: And for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it ascends and skirts the river.

cards.note: *And Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west . of him for Put, and to the west of him and to the west thereof on the sea for Canaan.* (Jubilees 9:1). *And the children of Ham were Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan according to their generation and cities.* (Jasher 10:19). Jasher names Ham's four sons; Jubilees shows Ham dividing his portion among those same four, laid out from east to west: Cush to the east, then Mizraim, then Put, then Canaan on the sea. One book is the roll call and the other is the map. Canaan's lot on the sea matters later, because Canaan did not keep to it but settled in Shem's portion, and the land that bears his name was never his by right.
cards.s_text: And the children of Ham were Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan according to their generation and cities.
cards.t_text: And Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west . of him for Put, and to the west of him and to the west thereof on the sea for Canaan.

cards.note: *And the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tînâ; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner portions of the north until it reaches to the sea of Mê’at.* (Jubilees 9:8). *And these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, Gomer, Magog, Medai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; these are the children of Japheth according to their generations.* (Jasher 10:7). Jasher lists Japheth's seven sons; Jubilees takes the first two of that list and places them on the ground, Gomer's portion east from the north side to the river Tina, Magog's the inner north as far as the sea of Meot. The same names, now with borders. The far north was Magog's lot from the division of the earth, which is worth remembering whenever the prophets speak of Magog and the north.
cards.s_text: And these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, Gomer, Magog, Medai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; these are the children of Japheth according to their generations.
cards.t_text: And the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tînâ; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner portions of the north until it reaches to the sea of Mê’at.

cards.note: *For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because Yahuah (God) did there confound all the language of the children of men, and from thence they were dispersed into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.* (Jubilees 10:25). *And when Yahuah (the Lord) had scattered the sons of men on account of their sin at the tower, behold they spread forth into many divisions, and all the sons of men were dispersed into the four corners of the earth.* (Jasher 10:2). Jasher opens with the result: the sons of men scattered for their sin at the tower into the four corners of the earth. Jubilees gives the means and the name: the language confounded at Shinar, so the place is called Babel, and from there they went out each to his own cities according to his language and his nation. Jasher's "many divisions" are Jubilees' languages. The scattering was judgment on the tower, and both books say so.
cards.s_text: And when Yahuah (the Lord) had scattered the sons of men on account of their sin at the tower, behold they spread forth into many divisions, and all the sons of men were dispersed into the four corners of the earth.
cards.t_text: For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because Yahuah (God) did there confound all the language of the children of men, and from thence they were dispersed into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.

cards.note: *And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.* (Jubilees 8:8). *And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.* (Jasher 10:1). Jasher 10 opens with Peleg's death in Abram's forty-eighth year, at two hundred and thirty-nine years old; Jubilees gives his birth and the reason for his name. The man whose name means division was born as the earth was being divided and died in the days of the man through whom it would be gathered into one seed. Two books tell the two ends of Peleg's life. The name given at his birth was the headline of his generation.
cards.s_text: And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:7 — *And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.* Jubilees gives the fearful father where Jasher gives the fearless son before Nimrod — the same idol-people who would slay the witness of truth.
cards.s_text: And the king said to Abram, What is this that you have done to your father and to his gods? And Abram answered the king in the words that he spoke to his father, and he said, The large god that was with them in the house did to them what you have heard.
cards.t_text: And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.”

cards.note: Jubilees 12:12 — *Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no man knew it.* Jubilees tells the same deed Jasher tells with the hatchet — the called seed destroying his father's gods, a second witness to the legend.
cards.s_text: And when Abram saw all these things his anger was kindled against his father, and he hastened and took a hatchet in his hand, and came to the chamber of the gods, and he broke all his father’s gods.
cards.t_text: And in the sixtieth year of the life of Abram, that is, in the fourth week, in the fourth year thereof, Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no man knew it.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:17 — *All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God).* Jubilees has the same Abram turning from the host of heaven to the Maker, the elect heart that Jasher shows knowing Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And Abram knew Yahuah (the Lord), and he went in his ways and instructions, and Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) was with him.
cards.t_text: And a word came into his heart and he said: "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search (them) out?

cards.note: Jubilees 12:2–4 — *What help and profit have we from those idols which you do worship, And before which you do bow yourself? For there is no spirit in them, For they are dumb forms, and a misleading of the heart. Worship them not: Worship the Elohim (God) of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth...* Abram's idol-polemic to his father, the same plea Jasher gives him to cast away the vain things and serve Yahuah (Jasher 12:68).
cards.s_text: Now therefore hearken to my voice, and let us arise and go to the land of Canaan, out of the reach of injury from Nimrod; and serve you Yahuah (the Lord) who created you in the earth and it will be well with you; and cast away all the vain things which you pursue.
cards.t_text: And he said, "What help and profit have we from those idols which you do worship, And before which you do bow yourself?

cards.note: Jubilees 12:9 — *And in the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in the seventh year thereof, Abram took to himself a wife, and her name was Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.* The same marriage of Abram to Sarai that Jasher records alongside Nahor's to Milca (Jasher 12:44).
cards.s_text: And at that time Nahor and Abram took to themselves wives, the daughters of their brother Haran; the wife of Nahor was Milca and the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai. And Sarai, wife of Abram, was barren; she had no offspring in those days.
cards.t_text: And in the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in the seventh year thereof, Abram took to himself a wife, and her name was Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:14 — *And Haran hasted to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees...* The same death of Haran by fire in the Chaldees that Jasher records, his heart not perfect with Yahuah (Jasher 12:26).
cards.s_text: And Haran died when they had cast him into the fire, and he was burned to ashes, for his heart was not perfect with Yahuah (the Lord); and those men who cast him into the fire, the flame of the fire spread over them, and they were burned, and twelve men of them died.
cards.t_text: And Haran hasted to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees.

cards.note: *And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week that he spoke to his father, and informed him that he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him.* (Jubilees 12:28). *And Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram, and all the souls of his household and went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan. And when they came as far as the land of Haran they remained there, for it was exceedingly good land for pasture, and of sufficient extent for those who accompanied them.* (Jasher 13:1). Jasher tells how Terah brought the family out of Ur as far as Haran and stayed because the pasture was good. Jubilees picks up at the end of that stay: Abram speaks to his father and tells him he is going on to Canaan to see it. Haran was meant as a stop and became a settlement, so the call to Canaan had to be answered from inside a comfortable place. Both books keep the same road and the same halt on it.
cards.s_text: And Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram, and all the souls of his household and went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan. And when they came as far as the land of Haran they remained there, for it was exceedingly good land for pasture, and of sufficient extent for those who accompanied them.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week that he spoke to his father, and informed him that he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (God) said to him: “To you and to your seed will I give this land.”* (Jubilees 13:3). *And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Abram when he came to the land of Canaan, and said to him, This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever, and I will make your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* (Jasher 13:7). At Abram's entry into Canaan both books have Yahuah (God) speak the same grant: this land to you and to your seed. Jasher expands it, forever, seed like the stars of heaven, all the lands you see; Jubilees gives it in one sentence. The land was given to a bloodline before that bloodline existed. Every later argument about who holds it begins at this word to Abram, not at any treaty.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Abram when he came to the land of Canaan, and said to him, This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever, and I will make your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) said to him: “To you and to your seed will I give this land.”

cards.note: Jubilees 13:17 — *And in the fourth year of this week Lot parted from him, and Lot dwelt in Sodom, and the men of Sodom were sinners exceedingly.* Jubilees records the same parting of Lot to Sodom that closes Jasher 15:46.
cards.s_text: And Lot went from Abram to that place, and he there pitched his tent and he dwelt in Sodom, and they were separated from each other.
cards.t_text: And in the fourth year of this week Lot parted from him, and Lot dwelt in Sodom, and the men of Sodom were sinners exceedingly.

cards.note: Jubilees 13:15 — *And Pharaoh gave back Sarai, the wife of Abram, and he sent him out of the land of Egypt, and he journeyed to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning.* The restoration and sending-out that Jasher 15:30 narrates.
cards.s_text: Now therefore here is your wife, take her and go from our land lest we all die on her account. And Pharaoh took more cattle, men servants and maid servants, and silver and gold, to give to Abram, and he returned to him Sarai his wife.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh gave back Sarai, the wife of Abram, and he sent him out of the land of Egypt, and he journeyed to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, to the place of the altar, with Ai on the east, and Bethel on the west, and he blessed Yahuah (God) his Elohim (God) who had brought him back in peace.

cards.note: Jubilees 13:13 — *And it came to pass when Pharaoh seized Sarai, the wife of Abram, that Yahuah (God) plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.* Jubilees retells the very plague Jasher 15:28 says smote Pharaoh on Sarai's account.
cards.s_text: And the king kept away from Sarai, and the plagues of the angel of Yahuah (the Lord) ceased from him and his household; and Pharaoh knew that he was smitten on account of Sarai, and the king was greatly astonished at this.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass when Pharaoh seized Sarai, the wife of Abram, that Yahuah (God) plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.

cards.note: Jubilees 13:11 — *And Abram went into Egypt in the third year of the week, and he dwelt in Egypt five years before his wife was torn away from him.* Jubilees retells the identical descent into Egypt that opens Jasher 15.
cards.s_text: And Abram and all belonging to him rose and went down to Egypt on account of the famine, and when they were at the brook Mitzraim they remained there some time to rest from the fatigue of the road.
cards.t_text: And Abram went into Egypt in the third year of the week, and he dwelt in Egypt five years before his wife was torn away from him.

cards.note: Jubilees 14:24 — *And he went in to her, and she conceived and bare him a son, and he called his name Ishmael, in the fifth year of this week; and this was the eighty-sixth year in the life of Abram.* Jubilees gives the same birth and the same eighty-sixth year of Abram's life that Jasher 16:36 records.
cards.s_text: And Hagar at that time returned to her master’s house, and at the end of days Hagar bare a son to Abram, and Abram called his name Ishmael; and Abram was eighty-six years old when he begat him.
cards.t_text: And he went in to her, and she conceived and bare him a son, and he called his name Ishmael, in the fifth year of this week; and this was the eighty-sixth year in the life of Abram.

cards.note: Jubilees 14:5 — *And he looked toward heaven, and beheld the stars. And He said to him: “So shall your seed be.”* Jubilees carries the same seed-as-stars vision that Jasher 16:20 sets in Hebron.
cards.s_text: At that time Yahuah (the Lord) again appeared to Abram in Hebron, and he said to him, Do not fear, your reward is very great before me, for I will not leave you, until I shall have multiplied you, and blessed you and made your seed like the stars in heaven, which cannot be measured nor numbered.
cards.t_text: And he looked toward heaven, and beheld the stars. And He said to him: “So shall your seed be.”

cards.note: Jubilees 13:29 — *I lift up my hands to the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is your, lest you should say I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me–Aner, Eschol, and Mamre.* Jubilees renders Abram's refusal in Jasher 16:16 with the same thread-to-shoe-latchet oath.
cards.s_text: And now therefore behold, here is all belonging to you, take it and go; as Yahuah (the Lord) lives I will not take from you from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread, excepting the expense of the food of those who went out with me to battle, as also the portions of the men who went with me, Anar, Ashcol, and Mamre, they and their men, as well as those also who had remained to watch the baggage, they shall take their portion of the spoil.
cards.t_text: And Abram said to him: “I lift up my hands to the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is your, lest you should say I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me–Aner, Eschol, and Mamre. These will take their portion.”

cards.note: Jubilees 13:23 — *And they took captive Sodom and Adam and Zeboim, and they took captive Lot also, the son of Abram’s brother, and all his possessions, and they went to Dan.* Jubilees retells the identical capture of Lot, confirming Jasher 16:6 across the patriarchal record.
cards.s_text: And they plundered all the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, and they also took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, and his property, and they seized all the goods of the cities of Sodom, and they went away; and Unic, Abram’s servant, who was in the battle, saw this, and told Abram all that the kings had done to the cities of Sodom, and that Lot was taken captive by them.
cards.t_text: And they took captive Sodom and Adam and Zeboim, and they took captive Lot also, the son of Abram’s brother, and all his possessions, and they went to Dan.

cards.note: Jubilees 15:28–29 — *And do you command the children of Yashar'el (Israel) and let them observe the sign of this covenant for their generations as an eternal ordinance, and they will not be rooted out of the land. For the command is ordained for a covenant, that they should observe it for ever among all the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Jubilees binds the eternal sign of Jasher 17:18 on all Israel forever.
cards.s_text: At eight days old shall it be circumcised, and this covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
cards.t_text: And do you command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and let them observe the sign of this covenant for their generations as an eternal ordinance, and they will not be rooted out of the land.

cards.note: Jubilees 15:12 — *And the child on the eighth day you will circumcise, every male throughout your generations, him that is born in the house, or whom you have bought with money from any stranger, whom you have acquired who is not of your seed.* Jubilees holds the same eighth-day ordinance Jasher 17:18 carries.
cards.s_text: At eight days old shall it be circumcised, and this covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
cards.t_text: And the child on the eighth day you will circumcise, every male throughout your generations, him that is born in the house, or whom you have bought with money from any stranger, whom you have acquired who is not of your seed.

cards.note: Jubilees 16:5 — *And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day...* the wickedness Jasher dramatizes in the Hedad tale is what Jubilees says brought fire and brimstone on the whole region of the Jordan.
cards.s_text: And they went away quarreling from the judge, when the people of Sodom heard them, and they gathered about them and they exclaimed against the stranger, and they drove him rashly from the city.
cards.t_text: And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day, even as lo I have declared to you all their works, that they are wicked and sinners exceedingly, and that they defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and work uncleanness on the earth.

cards.note: Jubilees 16:1 — *And on the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham, at the oak of Mamre, and we talked with him, and we announced to him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.* Jubilees narrates the identical Mamre visit and announcement of a son that Jasher 18:9 records.
cards.s_text: And when they had done eating one of them said to him, I will return to you according to the time of life, and Sarah your wife shall have a son.
cards.t_text: And on the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham, at the oak of Mamre, and we talked with him, and we announced to him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.

cards.note: Jubilees 15:30 — *For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, Yahuah (God) did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar'el (Israel) to be His people.* Ishmael is circumcised in the flesh yet the covenant seed runs through the chosen line, as Jubilees declares of this same household.
cards.s_text: And there was not one left whom he did not circumcise, and Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised in the flesh of their foreskin; thirteen years old was Ishmael when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
cards.t_text: For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, Yahuah (God) did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar’el (Israel) to be His people.

cards.note: Jubilees 16:6–7 — *And, in like manner, Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom. But Lot we saved; for Elohim (God) remembered Abraham, and sent him out from the midst of the overthrow.* Jubilees grounds Lot's deliverance, which Jasher records, in election — Elohim remembered Abraham (Jasher 19:57).
cards.s_text: And Lot and his two daughters remained in the cave, and they made their father drink wine, and they lay with him, for they said there was no man upon earth that could raise up seed from them, for they thought that the whole earth was destroyed.
cards.t_text: And, in like manner, Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom.

cards.note: Jubilees 16:5 — *And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day, even as lo I have declared to you all their works, that they are wicked and sinners exceedingly, and that they defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and work uncleanness on the earth.* Jubilees narrates the identical fire-and-brimstone overthrow Jasher records, the same patriarchal event from another witness (Jasher 19:51).
cards.s_text: Then Yahuah (the Lord) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah and upon all these cities brimstone and fire from Yahuah (the Lord) out of heaven.
cards.t_text: And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day, even as lo I have declared to you all their works, that they are wicked and sinners exceedingly, and that they defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and work uncleanness on the earth.

cards.note: *And in this month Abraham moved from Hebron, and departed and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur in the mountains of Gerar.* (Jubilees 16:10). *And at that time Abraham journeyed from the plain of Mamre, and he went to the land of the Philistines, and he dwelt in Gerar; it was in the twenty-fifth year of Abraham’s being in the land of Canaan, and the hundredth year of the life of Abraham, that he came to Gerar in the land of the Philistines.* (Jasher 20:1). Both books move Abraham from the plain of Mamre to Gerar at the same point in the story. Jubilees dates it by the month and places him between Kadesh and Shur in the mountains of Gerar; Jasher dates it to his hundredth year, the twenty-fifth in Canaan, and names the land as the Philistines'. The year of Isaac's birth is the year of the move. Sarah will be taken by Abimelech there, and both books are setting the stage.
cards.s_text: And at that time Abraham journeyed from the plain of Mamre, and he went to the land of the Philistines, and he dwelt in Gerar; it was in the twenty-fifth year of Abraham’s being in the land of Canaan, and the hundredth year of the life of Abraham, that he came to Gerar in the land of the Philistines.
cards.t_text: And in this month Abraham moved from Hebron, and departed and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur in the mountains of Gerar.

cards.note: Jubilees 17:4 — *And Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she became jealous of Ishmael and said to Abraham, "Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of this bondwoman will not be heir with my son, Isaac."* Jubilees narrates the same expulsion Jasher 21:16 records.
cards.s_text: And Abraham hearkened to the voice of Sarah, and he rose up early in the morning, and he took twelve loaves and a bottle of water which he gave to Hagar, and sent her away with her son, and Hagar went with her son to the wilderness, and they dwelt in the wilderness of Paran with the inhabitants of the wilderness, and Ishmael was an archer, and he dwelt in the wilderness a long time.
cards.t_text: And Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she became jealous of Ishmael and said to Abraham, “Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of this bondwoman will not be heir with my son, Isaac.”

cards.note: Jubilees 17:2 — *And Ishmael, the son of Hagar, the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham, his father, in his place, and Abraham rejoiced and blessed Elohim (God) because he had seen his sons.* The same gathered rejoicing Jasher 21:6 reports of Terah and Nahor coming up to the feast.
cards.s_text: Also Terah, the father of Abraham, and Nahor his brother, came from Haran, they and all belonging to them, for they greatly rejoiced on hearing that a son had been born to Sarah.
cards.t_text: And Ishmael, the son of Hagar, the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham, his father, in his place, and Abraham rejoiced and blessed Elohim (God) because he had seen his sons and had not died childless.

cards.note: Jubilees 17:1 — *And in the first year of the fifth week Isaac was weaned in this jubilee, and Abraham made a great banquet in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.* Jubilees dates the same banquet Jasher describes.
cards.s_text: And the child grew up and he was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast upon the day that Isaac was weaned.
cards.t_text: And in the first year of the fifth week Isaac was weaned in this jubilee, and Abraham made a great banquet in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.

cards.note: Jubilees 16:14 — *And Abraham circumcised his son on the eighth day: he was the first that was circumcised according to the covenant which is ordained for ever.* Jubilees marks the same eighth-day sign as the covenant ordained forever.
cards.s_text: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac at eight days old, as Elohim had commanded Abraham to do to his seed after him; and Abraham was one hundred, and Sarah ninety years old, when Isaac was born to them.
cards.t_text: And Abraham circumcised his son on the eighth day: he was the first that was circumcised according to the covenant which is ordained for ever.

cards.note: Jubilees 16:15 — *And in the sixth year of the fourth week we came to Abraham, to the Well of the Oath, and we appeared to him as we had told Sarah that we should return to her, and she would have conceived a son.* Jubilees narrates the very visitation Jasher 21:1 retells.
cards.s_text: And it was at that time at the end of a year and four months of Abraham’s dwelling in the land of the Philistines in Gerar, that Elohim (God) visited Sarah, and Yahuah (the Lord) remembered her, and she conceived and bare a son to Abraham.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the fourth week we came to Abraham, to the Well of the Oath, and we appeared to him as we had told Sarah that we should return to her, and she would have conceived a son.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (God) knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions; for He had tried him through his country and with famine, and had tried him with the wealth of kings, and had tried him again through his wife, when she was torn (from him), and with circumcision, and had tried him through Ishmael and Hagar, his maid-servant, when he sent them away.* (Jubilees 17:17). *And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the word that Isaac spoke to Ishmael, and it seemed good in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he thought to try Abraham in this matter.* (Jasher 22:45). Jasher explains how the test of Isaac came about: Yahuah (the Lord) heard Isaac's word to Ishmael and thought to try Abraham in this matter. Jubilees lists the trials already behind him, his country, famine, the wealth of kings, his wife torn from him, circumcision, Ishmael and Hagar sent away, and says Yahuah (God) knew he was faithful. The test on the mountain was not to discover something unknown. It was the next in a series Abraham had already been passing, and the one who tried him knew him before he tried him.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the word that Isaac spoke to Ishmael, and it seemed good in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he thought to try Abraham in this matter.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions; for He had tried him through his country and with famine, and had tried him with the wealth of kings, and had tried him again through his wife, when she was torn (from him), and with circumcision, and had tried him through Ishmael and Hagar, his maid-servant, when he sent them away.

cards.note: *And in the middle of the fifth month he moved from thence, and dwelt at the Well of the Oath.* (Jubilees 16:11). *And Abimelech took the seven ewe lambs which Abraham had given to him, for he had also given him cattle and herds in abundance, and Abimelech swore to Abraham concerning the well, therefore he called that well Beersheba, for there they both swore concerning it.* (Jasher 22:9). Jubilees calls the place by what happened there: the Well of the Oath. Jasher tells what the oath was, Abimelech swearing to Abraham over the well, the seven ewe lambs as witness, and the name Beersheba given because both swore. Jubilees dates Abraham's move there to the middle of the fifth month; Jasher explains why the well carried a name at all. Beersheba means a sworn well, and both books are leaning on the same story.
cards.s_text: And Abimelech took the seven ewe lambs which Abraham had given to him, for he had also given him cattle and herds in abundance, and Abimelech swore to Abraham concerning the well, therefore he called that well Beersheba, for there they both swore concerning it.
cards.t_text: And in the middle of the fifth month he moved from thence, and dwelt at the Well of the Oath.

cards.note: Jubilees 18:18 — *And he celebrated this festival every year, seven days with joy, and he called it the festival of Yahuah (God) according to the seven days during which he went and returned in peace.* Jubilees turns the same accepted offering of Jasher 23:70 into an ordained seven-day feast — Torah-before-Sinai, the fathers keeping the appointed time.
cards.s_text: And Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold, a ram was caught in a thicket by his horns; that was the ram which Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) had created in the earth in the day that he made earth and heaven.
cards.t_text: And he celebrated this festival every year, seven days with joy, and he called it the festival of Yahuah (God) according to the seven days during which he went and returned in peace.

cards.note: Jubilees 18:12 — *And the prince of the Mastêmâ was put to shame; and Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, a single ram caught … by his horns...* Jubilees gives the adversary Jasher calls Satan the name Mastema, and shows him shamed at the same altar where Abraham resists him in Jasher 23:33.
cards.s_text: And Abraham answered his son Isaac and said to him, Take heed of him and do not listen to his words, nor attend to him, for he is Satan, endeavoring to draw us aside this day from the commands of Elohim.
cards.t_text: And the prince of the Mastêmâ was put to shame; and Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, a single ram caught … by his horns, and Abraham went and took the ram and offered it for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.

cards.note: *And He said, “Take your beloved son whom you love, (even) Isaac, and go to the high country, and offer him on one of the mountains which I will point out to you.”* (Jubilees 18:2). *At that time the word of Yahuah (the Lord) came to Abraham, and he said to him, Abraham, and he said, Here I am.* (Jasher 23:1). Jasher gives the call: the word of Yahuah (the Lord) came, "Abraham," and he answered, "Here I am." Jubilees gives what the word said: take your beloved son, Isaac, go to the high country, and offer him on a mountain I will show you. One book has the summons and the other the command. "Here I am" was spoken before Abraham knew what was going to be asked, which is the whole shape of his faith.
cards.s_text: At that time the word of Yahuah (the Lord) came to Abraham, and he said to him, Abraham, and he said, Here I am.
cards.t_text: And He said, “Take your beloved son whom you love, (even) Isaac, and go to the high country, and offer him on one of the mountains which I will point out to you.”

cards.note: *And in the first year of the third week of this jubilee the days of the life of Sarah were accomplished, and she died in Hebron.* (Jubilees 19:2). *And at her bier was Shem, his sons Eber and Abimelech, together with Anar, Ashcol and Mamre, and all the grandees of the land followed her bier.* (Jasher 24:14). Jubilees records Sarah's death with its date, the first year of the third week of the jubilee, at Hebron. Jasher shows who came to her bier: Shem, with Eber and Abimelech, Anar, Ashcol and Mamre, and all the grandees of the land. Shem was still alive to bury Sarah; the generation of the ark and the generation of the promise overlapped. The woman through whom the seed came was followed to her grave by the man who came through the flood.
cards.s_text: And at her bier was Shem, his sons Eber and Abimelech, together with Anar, Ashcol and Mamre, and all the grandees of the land followed her bier.
cards.t_text: And in the first year of the third week of this jubilee the days of the life of Sarah were accomplished, and she died in Hebron.

cards.note: Jubilees 19:17 — *For he shall be in my stead on the earth, And for a blessing in the midst of the children of men, And for the glory of the whole seed of Shem.* Isaac is sent to Shem's house to learn the ways of Yahuah (Jasher 24:17); Jubilees names the same Shem-line as the glory through which the chosen seed is blessed.
cards.s_text: And when the days of their mourning passed by Abraham sent away his son Isaac, and he went to the house of Shem and Eber, to learn the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) and his instructions, and Abraham remained there three years.
cards.t_text: And he said to her: "My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, For he shall be in my stead on the earth, And for a blessing in the midst of the children of men, And for the glory of the whole seed of Shem.

cards.note: *This is the tenth trial wherewith Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit.* (Jubilees 19:8). *And the life of Sarah was one hundred and twenty-seven years, and Sarah died; and Abraham rose up from before his dead to seek a burial place to bury his wife Sarah; and he went and spoke to the children of Heth, the inhabitants of the land, saying,* (Jasher 24:1). Jasher tells it plainly: Sarah died at a hundred and twenty-seven, and Abraham rose up from before his dead to seek a burial place from the children of Heth. Jubilees counts that same errand as the tenth trial, and says he was found faithful and patient in spirit. Buying a grave in a land he had been promised and did not yet own, from the men who held it, without complaint, was a test, and Jubilees says he passed it. Faith is not only on the mountain with the knife; it is also in the field with the silver.
cards.s_text: And the life of Sarah was one hundred and twenty-seven years, and Sarah died; and Abraham rose up from before his dead to seek a burial place to bury his wife Sarah; and he went and spoke to the children of Heth, the inhabitants of the land, saying,
cards.t_text: This is the tenth trial wherewith Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit.

cards.note: Jubilees 19:13 — *And in the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Rebecca bare to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau, and Jacob was a smooth and upright man, and Esau was fierce, a man of the field, and hairy, and Jacob dwelt in tents.* The parallel record carries Rebecca's barren womb of Jasher 25:28 forward to the elect twins it will bear.
cards.s_text: And Rebecca the daughter of Bethuel, the wife of Abraham’s son Isaac, was barren in those days, she had no offspring; and Isaac dwelt with his father in the land of Canaan; and Yahuah (the Lord) was with Isaac; and Arpachshad the son of Shem the son of Noah died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Isaac, and all the days that Arpachshad lived were four hundred and thirty-eight years, and he died.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Rebecca bare to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau, and Jacob was a smooth and upright man, and Esau was fierce, a man of the field, and hairy, and Jacob dwelt in tents.

cards.note: Jubilees 20:10–11 — *And you will be for a blessing on the earth, And all nations of the earth will desire you, And bless your sons in my name, That they may be blessed as I am.” And he gave to Ishmael and to his sons, and to the sons of Keturah, gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, and he gave everything to Isaac his son.* The parallel record gives the same verdict as Jasher 25:6 — gifts to the branches, everything to Isaac.
cards.s_text: And Abraham sent all these away, and he gave them gifts, and they went away from his son Isaac to dwell wherever they should find a place.
cards.t_text: And you will be for a blessing on the earth, And all nations of the earth will desire you, And bless your sons in my name, That they may be blessed as I am.”

cards.note: Jubilees 19:11–12 — *And Abraham took to himself a third wife, and her name was Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah. And she bare him six sons, Zimram, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, in the two weeks of years.* The same Keturah-and-six-sons scene in the parallel patriarchal record beside Jasher 25:2.
cards.s_text: And she bare to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, being six sons. And the children of Zimran were Abihen, Molich and Narim.
cards.t_text: And Abraham took to himself a third wife, and her name was Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah.

cards.note: Jubilees 19:17–18 — *My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, For he shall be in my stead on the earth, And for a blessing in the midst of the children of men, And for the glory of the whole seed of Shem. For I know that Yahuah (God) will choose him to be a people for possession to Himself, above all peoples that are upon the face of the earth.* Where Jasher 26:28 has Abraham bless Isaac and teach Jacob the way of Yahuah, Jubilees fixes the election squarely on Jacob as the chosen seed.
cards.s_text: And Isaac answered his father and said to him, That which my Lord has commanded that will I do, and I will not depart from the commands of Yahuah my Elohim (the Lord my God), I will keep all that he commanded me; and Abraham blessed his son Isaac, and also his children; and Abraham taught Jacob the instruction of Yahuah (the Lord) and his ways.
cards.t_text: And he said to her: "My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, For he shall be in my stead on the earth, And for a blessing in the midst of the children of men, And for the glory of the whole seed of Shem.

cards.note: *And it came to pass in the first week in the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, that is, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the feast of weeks–that is, the feast of the first-fruits of the harvest–to Abraham, their father, and Abraham rejoiced because his two sons had come.* (Jubilees 22:1). *And all the inhabitants of the land of Haran, and all the families of the house of Abraham, and all the princes and grandees, and the sons of Abraham by the concubines, all came when they heard of Abraham’s death, and they requited Abraham’s kindness, and comforted Isaac his son, and they buried Abraham in the cave which he bought from Ephron the Hittite and his children, for the possession of a burial place.* (Jasher 26:31). Jubilees shows the last feast of weeks of Abraham's life, with Isaac and Ishmael both come to him from the Well of the Oath, and the old man glad to have his two sons together. Jasher shows the funeral: all Haran, all the house, the princes, and the sons of the concubines, burying him in the cave bought from Ephron. The feast and the burial sit in the same year. Both sons were at the table before they were at the grave, and Abraham died having kept the feast.
cards.s_text: And all the inhabitants of the land of Haran, and all the families of the house of Abraham, and all the princes and grandees, and the sons of Abraham by the concubines, all came when they heard of Abraham’s death, and they requited Abraham’s kindness, and comforted Isaac his son, and they buried Abraham in the cave which he bought from Ephron the Hittite and his children, for the possession of a burial place.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in the first week in the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, that is, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the feast of weeks–that is, the feast of the first-fruits of the harvest–to Abraham, their father, and Abraham rejoiced because his two sons had come.

cards.note: Jubilees 19:14–15 — *And the youths grew, and Jacob learned to write; but Esau did not learn, for he was a man of the field and a hunter, and he learnt war, and all his deeds were fierce. And Abraham loved Jacob, but Isaac loved Esau.* The same growing-up of the twins that Jasher 26:17 frames as Jacob learning the way of Yahuah while Esau hunted.
cards.s_text: And the boys grew up to their fifteenth year, and they came amongst the society of men. Esau was a designing and deceitful man, and an expert hunter in the field, and Jacob was a man perfect and wise, dwelling in tents, feeding flocks and learning the instructions of Yahuah (the Lord) and the commands of his father and mother.
cards.t_text: And the youths grew, and Jacob learned to write; but Esau did not learn, for he was a man of the field and a hunter, and he learnt war, and all his deeds were fierce.

cards.note: *And in the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Rebecca bare to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau, and Jacob was a smooth and upright man, and Esau was fierce, a man of the field, and hairy, and Jacob dwelt in tents.* (Jubilees 19:13). *And after that came his brother, and his hand took hold of Esau’s heel, therefore they called his name Jacob.* (Jasher 26:15). Jasher gives the birth: the second came out with his hand on Esau's heel, so they called him Jacob. Jubilees gives the birth and then the men the two became, Jacob smooth and upright, dwelling in tents, Esau fierce and hairy, a man of the field. The division between the brothers began at the womb and showed in how they lived. Two sons of one mother, and only one of them called upright, and the book says so before the birthright is ever sold.
cards.s_text: And after that came his brother, and his hand took hold of Esau’s heel, therefore they called his name Jacob.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Rebecca bare to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau, and Jacob was a smooth and upright man, and Esau was fierce, a man of the field, and hairy, and Jacob dwelt in tents.

cards.note: Jubilees 24:4 — *And Esau said in his heart: “I shall die; of what profit to me is this birthright?” And he said to Jacob: “I give it to you.”* Jubilees narrates the same birthright sale after Abraham's death that Jasher 27:12 records.
cards.s_text: And he said to his brother Jacob, Behold I shall die this day, and therefore then do I want the birthright? And Jacob acted wisely with Esau in this matter, and Esau sold his birthright to Jacob, for it was so brought about by Yahuah (the Lord).
cards.t_text: And Esau said in his heart: “I shall die; of what profit to me is this birthright?” And he said to Jacob: “I give it to you.”

cards.note: Jubilees 24:15 — *And he sowed in the land of the Philistines and brought in a hundred-fold, and Isaac became exceedingly great, and the Philistines envied him.* Jubilees records the same hundredfold sowing as Jasher 28:14, the parallel patriarchal witness.
cards.s_text: And Isaac sowed in that land, and received a hundred-fold in the same year, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed him.
