cards.t_text: And he sowed in the land of the Philistines and brought in a hundred-fold, and Isaac became exceedingly great, and the Philistines envied him.

cards.note: Jubilees 24:2 — *And in the first year of the fourth week a famine began in the land, besides the first famine, which had been in the days of Abraham.* Jubilees narrates the identical post-Abraham famine, a genuine self-link to Jasher 28:1 in the patriarchal record.
cards.s_text: And in those days, after the death of Abraham, in that year Yahuah (the Lord) brought a heavy famine in the land, and whilst the famine was raging in the land of Canaan, Isaac rose up to go down to Egypt on account of the famine, as his father Abraham had done.
cards.t_text: And in the first year of the fourth week a famine began in the land, besides the first famine, which had been in the days of Abraham.

cards.note: Jubilees 27:11 — *And El Shaddai (God Almighty) bless you and increase and multiply you that you may become a company of nations, and give you the blessings of my father Abraham, to you and to your seed after you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings and all the land which Elohim (God) gave to Abraham: go, my son, in peace.* The Jubilees telling of the same Abrahamic blessing Isaac gives in Jasher 29:29.
cards.s_text: And may Elohim (God) give to you and your seed the blessing of your father Abraham, and make you fruitful and multiply you, and may you become a multitude of people in the land whither you go, and may Elohim cause you to return to this land, the land of your father’s dwelling, with children and with great riches, with joy and with pleasure.
cards.t_text: And El Shaddai (God Almighty) bless you and increase and multiply you that you may become a company of nations, and give you the blessings of my father Abraham, to you and to your seed after you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings and all the land which Elohim (God) gave to Abraham: go, my son, in peace.”

cards.note: Jubilees 27:3 — *Now, therefore, my son, obey my voice, and arise and flee you to Laban, my brother, to Haran, and tarry with him a few days until your brother’s anger turns away, and he remove his anger from you, and forget all that you have done; then I will send and fetch you from thence.* The Jubilees telling of Rebecca's same charge to flee to Haran, paralleling Jasher 29:23.
cards.s_text: And this was told to Rebecca, and she hastened and sent and called for Jacob her son, and she said to him, Arise, go and flee to Haran to my brother Laban, and remain there for some time, until your brother’s anger be turned from you and then shall you come back.
cards.t_text: Now, therefore, my son, obey my voice, and arise and flee you to Laban, my brother, to Haran, and tarry with him a few days until your brother’s anger turns away, and he remove his anger from you, and forget all that you have done; then I will send and fetch you from thence.”

cards.note: Jubilees 26:13 — *And Jacob went in to his father and said: “I am your son: I have done according as you bade me: arise and sit and eat of that which I have caught, father, that your soul may bless me.”* The Jubilees telling of the same scene, the third witness to Jasher 29:7.
cards.s_text: And Isaac said to Jacob, Who are you, my son? And he said, I am your first born Esau, I have done as you did order me, now therefore rise up I pray you, and eat of my hunt, in order that your soul may bless me as you did speak to me.
cards.t_text: And Jacob went in to his father and said: “I am your son: I have done according as you bade me: arise and sit and eat of that which I have caught, father, that your soul may bless me.”

cards.note: Jubilees 29:18 — *For in the days when Jacob went to Mesopotamia, Esau took to himself a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, and he gathered together all the flocks of his father and his wives, and went up and dwelt on Mount Seir, and left Isaac his father at the Well of the Oath alone.* Jubilees sets Esau's move to Seir in the same span Jasher 30:27 does — while Jacob serves Laban.
cards.s_text: And when Esau saw that his quarreling increased with the inhabitants of the land of Canaan, he rose up and took his wives and his sons and his daughters, and all belonging to him, and the cattle which he possessed, and all his property that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and he went away from the inhabitants of the land to the land of Seir, and Esau and all belonging to him dwelt in the land of Seir.
cards.t_text: For in the days when Jacob went to Mesopotamia, Esau took to himself a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, and he gathered together all the flocks of his father and his wives, and went up and dwelt on Mount Seir, and left Isaac his father at the Well of the Oath alone.

cards.note: Jubilees 28:1 — *And he went on his journey, and came to the land of the east, to Laban, the brother of Rebecca, and he was with him, and served him for Rachel his daughter one week.* Jubilees narrates the same service-for-Rachel that Jasher 30:14 sets at seven years.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to Laban, I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter; and Laban consented to this and Jacob served Laban seven years for his daughter Rachel.
cards.t_text: And he went on his journey, and came to the land of the east, to Laban, the brother of Rebecca, and he was with him, and served him for Rachel his daughter one week.

cards.note: Jubilees 27:21 — *And he dreamt that night, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and behold, the angels of Yahuah (God) ascended and descended on it: and behold, Yahuah (God) stood upon it...* Jubilees narrates the identical Bethel night that Jasher 30:1-3 retells.
cards.s_text: And Jacob awoke from his sleep and he rejoiced greatly at the vision which he had seen; and he called the name of that place Bethel.
cards.t_text: And he dreamt that night, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and behold, the angels of Yahuah (God) ascended and descended on it: and behold, Yahuah (God) stood upon it.

cards.note: Jubilees 28:4 — *And he went in to her, and behold, she was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban, and said to him: “Why have you dealt thus with me? Did not I serve you for Rachel and not for Leah?* Jubilees narrates the same deceived wedding night that Jasher 31:4 tells, the two extra-canon witnesses agreeing with Genesis.
cards.s_text: And afterward Laban took his daughter Leah, and he brought her to Jacob, and he came to her and Jacob did not know that she was Leah.
cards.t_text: And he went in to her, and behold, she was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban, and said to him: “Why have you dealt thus with me? Did not I serve you for Rachel and not for Leah? Why have you wronged me? Take your daughter, and I will go; for you have done evil to me.”

cards.note: Jubilees 28:11 — *And Yahuah (God) opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bare Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.* Jubilees dates the first of the sons Jasher 31:15 lists, the same tribal beginning.
cards.s_text: And these are their names, Reuben Simeon, Levi, and Judah, and she afterward left bearing.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bare Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.

cards.note: Jubilees 28:24 — *And Yahuah (God) was gracious to Rachel, and opened her womb, and she conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year in this fourth week.* Jubilees dates the birth that answers Rachel's prayer in Jasher 31:19.
cards.s_text: And Rachel was still barren in those days, and Rachel prayed to Yahuah (the Lord) at that time, and she said, O Yahuah Elohim (O Lord God) remember me and visit me, I beseech you, for now my husband will cast me off, for I have borne him no children.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) was gracious to Rachel, and opened her womb, and she conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year in this fourth week.

cards.note: Jubilees 28:29–30 — *And Jacob's possessions multiplied exceedingly, and he possessed oxen and sheep and asses and camels, and menservants and maidservants. And Laban and his sons envied Jacob.* Jubilees joins the same multiplying-and-envy Jasher 31:31-35 records.
cards.s_text: And Jacob served Laban six years longer, and when the sheep brought forth, Jacob removed from them such as were speckled and spotted, as he had determined with Laban, and Jacob did so at Laban’s for six years, and the man increased abundantly and he had cattle and maid servants and men servants, camels, and asses.
cards.t_text: And Jacob’s possessions multiplied exceedingly, and he possessed oxen and sheep and asses and camels, and menservants and maidservants.

cards.note: Jubilees 29:2 — *And Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and spake kindly to them that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.* Jubilees narrates the same shearing-day flight Jasher 31:37-40 sets up.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob at the expiration of the six years, and said to him, Arise, go forth out of this land, and return to the land of your birthplace and I will be with you.
cards.t_text: And Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and spake kindly to them that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.

cards.note: Jubilees 29:8 — *And he made there a heap for a witness; wherefore the name of that place is called: “The Heap of Witness,” after this heap.* Jubilees names the same Gilead heap-of-witness Jacob and Laban raise in Jasher 31:52.
cards.s_text: And they took stones and made a heap, and Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and you, therefore he called the name of it Gilead.
cards.t_text: And he made there a heap for a witness; wherefore the name of that place is called: “The Heap of Witness,” after this heap.

cards.note: *And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.* (Jubilees 29:13). *And Esau hearkened to the voice of Jacob, and Esau returned with the four hundred men that were with him on their road to Seir, and Jacob and all belonging to him went that day as far as the extremity of the land of Canaan in its borders, and he remained there some time.* (Jasher 32:73). Jubilees dates the crossing of the Jabbok and puts the meeting with Esau on the same day: reconciled, and then parted, Esau to Seir and Jacob to his tents. Jasher tells the parting from the road: Esau heard Jacob's voice and turned back with his four hundred men toward Seir while Jacob went on to the edge of Canaan. Peace between the brothers did not make them one house. Esau went his way with his army and Jacob stayed a dweller in tents, and the two lines stayed two lines.
cards.s_text: And Esau hearkened to the voice of Jacob, and Esau returned with the four hundred men that were with him on their road to Seir, and Jacob and all belonging to him went that day as far as the extremity of the land of Canaan in its borders, and he remained there some time.
cards.t_text: And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:18 — *And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before Yahuah (God), as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Yashar'el (Israel).* Jubilees reads Levi's resolve in Jasher 33:39 as the zeal that won him the priesthood.
cards.s_text: And Simeon’s advice pleased them, and Simeon and Levi resolved to do to them as it was proposed.
cards.t_text: And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before Yahuah (God), as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Jubilees 30:6 — *And Yahuah (God) delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob that they might exterminate them with the sword and execute judgment upon them, and that it might not thus again be done in Yashar'el (Israel) that a virgin of Yashar'el (Israel) should be defiled.* Jubilees names the same hand that Jasher 33:52 names — Yahuah delivering Shechem into the sons of Jacob.
cards.s_text: And they circumcised Shechem and Hamor his father, and the five brothers of Shechem, and then every one rose up and went home, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) against the city of Shechem, and from Yahuah (the Lord) was Simeon’s counsel in this matter, in order that Yahuah (the Lord) might deliver the city of Shechem into the hands of Jacob’s two sons.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob that they might exterminate them with the sword and execute judgment upon them, and that it might not thus again be done in Yashar’el (Israel) that a virgin of Yashar’el (Israel) should be defiled.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:5 — *And thus let it not again be done from henceforth that a daughter of Yashar'el (Israel) be defiled; for judgment is ordained in heaven against them that they should destroy with the sword all the men of the Shechemites because they had wrought shame in Yashar'el (Israel).* Jubilees draws from this scene the same standing judgment Jasher 33:34 invokes against the city.
cards.s_text: And when they had gone, the sons of Jacob said to their father, saying, Behold, we know that death is due to these wicked ones and to their city, because they transgressed that which Elohim (God) had commanded to Noah and his children and his seed after them.
cards.t_text: And thus let it not again be done from henceforth that a daughter of Yashar’el (Israel) be defiled; for judgment is ordained in heaven against them that they should destroy with the sword all the men of the Shechemites because they had wrought shame in Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Jubilees 30:2 — *And there they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite, the prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her, and she was a little girl, a child of twelve years.* Jubilees, like Jasher 33:11, has Dinah carried into Shechem's house and defiled.
cards.s_text: And he sent and had her taken by force, and Dinah came to the house of Shechem and he seized her forcibly and lay with her and humbled her, and he loved her exceedingly and placed her in his house.
cards.t_text: And there they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite, the prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her, and she was a little girl, a child of twelve years.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:1 — *And in the first year of the sixth week he went up to Salem, to the east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month.* Jubilees fixes Jacob's coming to Shalem/Shechem in its calendar, the same scene Jasher 33:1 opens with.
cards.s_text: And in some time after Jacob went away from the borders of the land, and he came to the land of Shalem, that is the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, and he rested in front of the city.
cards.t_text: And in the first year of the sixth week he went up to Salem, to the east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:26 — *And the dread of Yahuah (God) was upon all the cities which are around about Shechem, and they did not rise to pursue after the sons of Jacob; for terror had fallen upon them.* Jubilees turns the surrounding cities' terror into the same shield over the sons of Jacob that blunts the seven kings of Jasher 34:50.
cards.s_text: And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled with all their armies, about ten thousand men with drawn swords, and they came to fight against the sons of Jacob; and Jacob heard that the kings of the Amorites had assembled to fight against his sons, and Jacob was greatly afraid, and it distressed him.
cards.t_text: And the dread of Yahuah (God) was upon all the cities which are around about Shechem, and they did not rise to pursue after the sons of Jacob; for terror had fallen upon them.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:25 — *And he reproached them because they had put the city to the sword; for he feared those who dwelt in the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.* Jacob's reproach and fear of the Canaanites and Perizzites in Jasher 34:33 stands word-for-word in Jubilees.
cards.s_text: And now you have done to make me obnoxious to the inhabitants of the land, amongst the Canaanites and the Perizzites, and I am but of a small number, and they will all assemble against me and slay me when they hear of your work with their brethren, and I and my household will be destroyed.
cards.t_text: And he reproached them because they had put the city to the sword; for he feared those who dwelt in the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:24 — *And they brought Dinah, their sister, out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive everything that was in Shechem, their sheep and their oxen and their asses, and all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought them all to Jacob their father.* The same flocks and captives Jasher 34:31 leads home to Jacob.
cards.s_text: And they took away their sheep and their oxen and their cattle, and also the remainder of the women and little ones, and they led all these away, and they opened a gate and went out and came to their father Jacob with vigor.
cards.t_text: And they brought Dinah, their sister, out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive everything that was in Shechem, their sheep and their oxen and their asses, and all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought them all to Jacob their father.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:4 — *And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and slew all the men whom they found in it, and left not a single one remaining in it: they slew all in torments because they had dishonoured their sister Dinah.* The same scene Jasher 34:25 tells, read in Jubilees as judgment for the defiled seed.
cards.s_text: And Simeon and Levi continued to go about in the city, and they killed all the people of the city at the edge of the sword, and they left none remaining.
cards.t_text: And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and slew all the men whom they found in it, and left not a single one remaining in it: they slew all in torments because they had dishonoured their sister Dinah.

cards.note: Jubilees 17:16 — *And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before Elohim (God), "Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and You will see if he will do this command, and You will know if he is faithful in everything wherein You do try him."* Jasher 35:11's love-driven offering of the only son is the same trial Jubilees frames as the testing of Abraham's faithfulness.
cards.s_text: And behold through his love toward his Elohim, Abraham took his only and precious son and intended to bring him up as a burnt offering to his Elohim, and had it not been for Elohim who prevented him from doing this, he would then have done it through his love to his Elohim.
cards.t_text: And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before Elohim (God), “Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and You will see if he will do this command, and You will know if he is faithful in everything wherein You do try him.”

cards.note: *And he abode that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained and made him the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), him and his sons for ever; and he awoke from his sleep and blessed Yahuah (God).* (Jubilees 32:1). *At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob saying, Arise, go to Bethel and remain there, and make there an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appears to you, who delivered you and your sons from affliction.* (Jasher 36:1). Jasher records the command to go up to Bethel and build an altar to the One who delivered him; Jubilees records what happened the night Jacob was there: Levi dreamed he had been ordained priest of the Most High, he and his sons for ever, and woke and blessed Yahuah (God). The altar Jacob was sent to build needed a priesthood, and the priesthood was given at Bethel in a dream long before Sinai named Levi. Jasher gives the summons to Bethel and Jubilees gives what Bethel produced.
cards.s_text: At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob saying, Arise, go to Bethel and remain there, and make there an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appears to you, who delivered you and your sons from affliction.
cards.t_text: And he abode that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained and made him the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), him and his sons for ever; and he awoke from his sleep and blessed Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *And in the night, on the twenty-third of this month, Deborah Rebecca’s nurse died, and they buried her beneath the city under the oak of the river, and he called the name of this place, “The river of Deborah,” and the oak, “The oak of the mourning of Deborah.”* (Jubilees 32:30). *And the life of Rebecca was one hundred and thirty-three years, and she died and when Jacob heard that his mother Rebecca was dead he wept bitterly for his mother, and made a great mourning for her, and for Deborah her nurse beneath the oak, and he called the name of that place Allon-bachuth.* (Jasher 36:6). Both books bury Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, under an oak and name the place for the mourning. Jubilees dates it to the twenty-third of the month and gives the names, the river of Deborah and the oak of the mourning of Deborah; Jasher calls the oak Allon-bachuth and sets it beside Jacob's weeping for his mother Rebecca, dead at a hundred and thirty-three. A nurse received a named oak and a dated grave. The books remembered the servants, not only the patriarchs.
cards.s_text: And the life of Rebecca was one hundred and thirty-three years, and she died and when Jacob heard that his mother Rebecca was dead he wept bitterly for his mother, and made a great mourning for her, and for Deborah her nurse beneath the oak, and he called the name of that place Allon-bachuth.
cards.t_text: And in the night, on the twenty-third of this month, Deborah Rebecca’s nurse died, and they buried her beneath the city under the oak of the river, and he called the name of this place, “The river of Deborah,” and the oak, “The oak of the mourning of Deborah.”

cards.note: *And Yahuah (God) appeared to him by night and blessed him and said to him: “Your name shall not be called Jacob, but Yashar’el (Israel) shall they name your name.”* (Jubilees 32:17). *And Jacob was a hundred years old when Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to him, and blessed him and called his name Israel, and Rachel the wife of Jacob conceived in those days.* (Jasher 36:8). Jasher says Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob when he was a hundred years old, blessed him, and called his name Israel; Jubilees gives the words of the blessing: your name shall not be called Jacob, but Yashar'el (Israel) shall they name your name. The name was not won in the wrestling alone; it was spoken by Yahuah (God) at Bethel by night. A people carries that name because it was placed on one man by the mouth of the One who appeared to him.
cards.s_text: And Jacob was a hundred years old when Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to him, and blessed him and called his name Israel, and Rachel the wife of Jacob conceived in those days.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) appeared to him by night and blessed him and said to him: “Your name shall not be called Jacob, but Yashar’el (Israel) shall they name your name.”

cards.note: Jubilees 32:34 — *And Rachel died there and she was buried in the land of Ephrath, the same is Bethlehem, and Jacob built a pillar on the grave of Rachel, on the road above her grave.* The same Ephrath/Bethlehem grave and pillar of Jasher 36:11.
cards.s_text: And Jacob buried her in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and he set a pillar upon her grave, which is there to this day; and the days of Rachel were forty-five years and she died.
cards.t_text: And Rachel died there and she was buried in the land of Ephrath, the same is Bethlehem, and Jacob built a pillar on the grave of Rachel, on the road above her grave.

cards.note: *And Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, the concubine of his father, bathing in water in a secret place, and he loved her.* (Jubilees 33:2). *And Reuben was jealous for his mother Leah on account of this, and he was filled with anger, and he rose up in his anger and went and entered the tent of Bilhah and he from there removed his father’s bed.* (Jasher 36:14). Jubilees shows the beginning: Reuben saw Bilhah bathing in a hidden place and wanted her. Jasher shows the motive and the deed: jealousy for his mother Leah, anger, and the removal of his father's bed from Bilhah's tent. One book gives the eye and the other the anger, and both end in the same sin against his father. Genesis 35:22 says it in a line; these two tell you how a firstborn lost his birthright.
cards.s_text: And Reuben was jealous for his mother Leah on account of this, and he was filled with anger, and he rose up in his anger and went and entered the tent of Bilhah and he from there removed his father’s bed.
cards.t_text: And Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, the concubine of his father, bathing in water in a secret place, and he loved her.

cards.note: *And these were the names of the sons of Jacob: the first-born Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Yahudah (Judah), Issachar, Zebulon, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali, and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, the daughter of Leah, the only daughter of Jacob.* (Jubilees 33:22). *And these are the generations of Jacob who were born to him in Padan-aram, and the sons of Jacob were twelve.* (Jasher 36:16). Jasher says the sons of Jacob were twelve; Jubilees names them by their mothers, Leah's six, Rachel's two, Bilhah's two, Zilpah's two, and adds Dinah, the only daughter. The roster matters because the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) are these twelve men and no others, and the gathering of the scattered seed is a gathering of these names. Jasher gives the count and Jubilees gives the list.
cards.s_text: And these are the generations of Jacob who were born to him in Padan-aram, and the sons of Jacob were twelve.
cards.t_text: And these were the names of the sons of Jacob: the first-born Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Yahudah (Judah), Issachar, Zebulon, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali, and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, the daughter of Leah, the only daughter of Jacob.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:6–7 — *And he arose from his housel he and his three sons and all the servants of his father, and his own servants, and he went against them with six thousand men, who carried swords. And he slew them in the pastures of Shechem, and pursued those who fled, and he slew them with the edge of the sword, and he slew ’Arêsa and Tâphû and Sarêgân and Sêlô and ’Amânîsakîr and Gâgâ’as, and he recovered his herds.* Jubilees compresses the whole battle Jasher 37:50 narrates king by king into one rout of the Amorite kings in the pastures of Shechem.
cards.s_text: And Elon with his captains approached nearer, and Levi looked back and saw that battle was given him in the rear, and Levi ran with twelve of his servants, and they went and slew Elon and his captains with the edge of the sword.
cards.t_text: And he arose from his housel he and his three sons and all the servants of his father, and his own servants, and he went against them with six thousand men, who carried swords.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:2 — *And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.* Jubilees narrates the identical gathering of the Amorite kings against the sons of Jacob that Jasher 37:6 sets at Shechem.
cards.s_text: And all the kings of Canaan again assembled, and they came together to make war with Jacob and his sons.
cards.t_text: And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:4 — *And there came the kings of Tâphû, and the kings of 'Arêsa, and the kings of Sêragân, and the kings of Sêlô, and the kings of Gâ'as, and the king of Bêthôrôn, and the king of Ma'anîsâkîr, and all those who dwell in these mountains (and) who dwell in the woods in the land of Canaan.* The king-roster of Sêlô and Bêthôrôn matches Jasher 38:6's Ihuri of Shiloh and Laban of Bethchorin slain by the bow.
cards.s_text: And he slew Parathon king of Chazar at the gate of the city of Chazar, and he afterward smote Susi king of Sarton, and Laban king of Bethchorin, and Shabir king of Machnaymah, and he slew them all with arrows, an arrow to each of them, and they died.
cards.t_text: And there came the kings of Tâphû, and the kings of ’Arêsa, and the kings of Sêragân, and the kings of Sêlô, and the kings of Gâ’as, and the king of Bêthôrôn, and the king of Ma’anîsâkîr, and all those who dwell in these mountains (and) who dwell in the woods in the land of Canaan.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:2 — *And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.* Jubilees gives the gathering of the Amorite kings against the seed that Jasher 38:2 shows already breaking and fleeing.
cards.s_text: And when Ihuri king of Shiloh was dead, the four remaining kings fled from their station with the rest of the captains, and they endeavored to retreat, saying, We have no more strength with the Hebrews after their having killed the three kings and their captains who were more powerful than we are.
cards.t_text: And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:6–7 — *And he arose from his housel he and his three sons and all the servants of his father, and his own servants, and he went against them with six thousand men, who carried swords. And he slew them in the pastures of Shechem, and pursued those who fled, and he slew them with the edge of the sword.* Jubilees tells the identical war of Jacob slaying the Amorite kings that Jasher 38:6 details king by king.
cards.s_text: And he slew Parathon king of Chazar at the gate of the city of Chazar, and he afterward smote Susi king of Sarton, and Laban king of Bethchorin, and Shabir king of Machnaymah, and he slew them all with arrows, an arrow to each of them, and they died.
cards.t_text: And he arose from his housel he and his three sons and all the servants of his father, and his own servants, and he went against them with six thousand men, who carried swords.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:8 — *And he prevailed over them, and imposed tribute on them that they should pay him tribute, five fruit products of their land, and he built Rôbêl and Tamnâtârês.* The victory and tribute Jubilees records is the same conquest Jasher 39 wins city by fortified city.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob came to Gaash and they found the gates of the city locked, and about five hundred men standing at the top of the outer-most wall, and a people numerous as the sand upon the sea shore were in ambush for the sons of Jacob from without the city at the rear of it.
cards.t_text: And he prevailed over them, and imposed tribute on them that they should pay him tribute, five fruit products of their land, and he built Rôbêl and Tamnâtârês

cards.note: Jubilees 34:4 — *And there came the kings of Tâphû, and the kings of ’Arêsa, and the kings of Sêragân, and the kings of Sêlô, and the kings of Gâ’as, and the king of Bêthôrôn, and the king of Ma’anîsâkîr, and all those who dwell in these mountains (and) who dwell in the woods in the land of Canaan.* Tâphû, Gâ’as and Sêlô are Jasher's Tapnach, Gaash and Shiloh — the same Amorite kings, named in both books.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob that day girt on their weapons of war, and they marched to battle against the inhabitants of Gaash, and in Gaash there was a strong and mighty people of the people of the Amorites, and Gaash was the strongest and best fortified city of all the cities of the Amorites, and it had three walls.
cards.t_text: And there came the kings of Tâphû, and the kings of ’Arêsa, and the kings of Sêragân, and the kings of Sêlô, and the kings of Gâ’as, and the king of Bêthôrôn, and the king of Ma’anîsâkîr, and all those who dwell in these mountains (and) who dwell in the woods in the land of Canaan.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:2 — *And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.* Jubilees compresses into one verse the gathering of the Amorite cities that Jasher 39 unfolds at Tapnach, Arbelan and Gaash.
cards.s_text: And on the fifth day the sons of Jacob heard that the people of Gaash had gathered against them to battle, because they had slain their king and their captains, for there had been fourteen captains in the city of Gaash, and the sons of Jacob had slain them all in the first battle.
cards.t_text: And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:9 — *And he returned in peace, and made peace with them, and they became his servants, until the day that he and his sons went down into Egypt.* Jubilees seals the war with the same lasting peace and servitude that Jasher carries until Israel inherits Canaan (Jasher 40:52).
cards.s_text: And there was peace from that day forward between the sons of Jacob and the kings of the Canaanites, until the children of Israel came to inherit the land of Canaan.
cards.t_text: And he returned in peace, and made peace with them, and they became his servants, until the day that he and his sons went down into Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:8 — *And he prevailed over them, and imposed tribute on them that they should pay him tribute, five fruit products of their land, and he built Rôbêl and Tamnâtârês.* The same imposed tribute Jasher records when the sons of Jacob make the Canaanite kings tributary from that day forward (Jasher 40:48).
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob swore to them that they would not meddle with them, and all the kings of the Canaanites swore also to them, and the sons of Jacob made them tributary from that day forward.
cards.t_text: And he prevailed over them, and imposed tribute on them that they should pay him tribute, five fruit products of their land, and he built Rôbêl and Tamnâtârês

cards.note: Jubilees 34:2 — *And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.* Jubilees narrates the identical war — the seven kings against Jacob's sons that Jasher draws out into the Bethchorin campaign and the kings' surrender (Jasher 40:22).
cards.s_text: And the seven kings of the Canaanites resolved to make peace with the sons of Jacob, for they were greatly afraid of their lives, on account of the sons of Jacob.
cards.t_text: And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled themselves together against them, to slay them, hiding themselves under the trees, and to take their cattle as a prey.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:10 — *And in the seventh year of this week he sent Joseph to learn about the welfare of his brothers from his house to the land of Shechem, and he found them in the land of Dothan.* The Jubilees retelling carries the same sending to Shechem and finding at Dothan that Jasher 41:23 records.
cards.s_text: And Joseph hearkened to the voice of the angel of Yahuah (the Lord), and he went to his brethren in Dothan and he found them in Dothan feeding the flock.
cards.t_text: And in the seventh year of this week he sent Joseph to learn about the welfare of his brothers from his house to the land of Shechem, and he found them in the land of Dothan.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:21–22 — *And Leah his wife died in the fourth year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee, and he buried her in the double cave near Rebecca his mother, to the left of the grave of Sarah, his father's mother. And all her sons and his sons came to mourn over Leah his wife with him, and to comfort him regarding her, for he was lamenting her.* The Jubilees retelling carries the same death and the same double cave that Jasher 41:3 places in Machpelah.
cards.s_text: And Jacob and his sons buried her in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which is in Hebron, which Abraham had bought from the children of Heth, for the possession of a burial place.
cards.t_text: And Leah his wife died in the fourth year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee, and he buried her in the double cave near Rebecca his mother, to the left of the grave of Sarah, his father’s mother.

cards.note: Genesis 37:28 — *Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.* The canon source standing beside both Jasher 42:24 and Jubilees 34:11 — one event, three witnesses.
cards.s_text: And they did so, and they reached the Ishmaelites, and the Midianites sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver which they had given for him to his brethren.
cards.t_text: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:11–12 — *And they dealt treacherously with him, and formed a plot against him to slay him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, priest of the city of 'Êlêw. And the sons of Jacob slaughtered a kid, and dipped the coat of Joseph in the blood, and sent (it) to Jacob their father on the tenth of the seventh month.* The same patriarchal sale Jasher 42:19 records — plot, change of mind, sold to the Ishmaelites down into Egypt.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob hearkened to the Midianites and they sold their brother Joseph to them for twenty pieces of silver, and Reuben their brother was not with them, and the Midianites took Joseph and continued their journey to Gilead.
cards.t_text: And they dealt treacherously with him, and formed a plot against him to slay him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, priest of the city of ’Êlêw.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:14 — *And his sons and his daughter rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted for his son.* Jubilees mirrors the refused comfort of Jasher 43:34.
cards.s_text: And all his sons and his servants and his servant’s children rose up and stood round him to comfort him, and he refused to be comforted.
cards.t_text: And his sons and his daughter rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted for his son.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:13 — *And he mourned all that night, for they had brought it to him in the evening, and he became feverish with mourning for his death, and he said: "An evil beast has devoured Joseph"; and all the members of his house mourned with him that day, and they were grieving and mourning with him all that day.* The live Jubilees layer keeps the identical "evil beast" cry of Jasher 43:20.
cards.s_text: And Jacob heard the words of his sons and he cried out with a loud voice, and he said, It is the coat of my son, an evil beast has devoured him; Joseph is rent in pieces, for I sent him this day to see whether it was well with you and well with the flocks and to bring me word again from you, and he went as I commanded him, and this has happened to him this day whilst I thought my son was with you.
cards.t_text: And he mourned all that night, for they had brought it to him in the evening, and he became feverish with mourning for his death, and he said: “An evil beast has devoured Joseph”; and all the members of his house mourned with him that day, and they were grieving and mourning with him all that day.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:18 — *For this reason it is ordained for the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they should afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month–on the day that the news which made him weep for Joseph came to Jacob his father–that they should make atonement for themselves thereon with a young goat on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved the affection of their father regarding Joseph his son.* Jubilees binds the kid's blood of Jasher 43:13 to the Day of Atonement — Torah and the appointed times stand, it ain't new.
cards.s_text: And they hastened and took Joseph’s coat and tore it, and they killed a kid of the goats and dipped the coat in the blood of the kid, and then trampled it in the dust, and they sent the coat to their father Jacob by the hand of Naphtali, and they commanded him to say these words:
cards.t_text: For this reason it is ordained for the children of Yashar’el (Israel) that they should afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month–on the day that the news which made him weep for Joseph came to Jacob his father–that they should make atonement for themselves thereon with a young goat on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved the affection of their father regarding Joseph his son.

cards.note: *And they dealt treacherously with him, and formed a plot against him to slay him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, priest of the city of ’Êlêw. And the sons of Jacob slaughtered a kid, and dipped the coat of Joseph in the blood, and sent (it) to Jacob their father on the tenth of the seventh month.* (Jubilees 34:11–12). *And they hastened and took Joseph’s coat and tore it, and they killed a kid of the goats and dipped the coat in the blood of the kid, and then trampled it in the dust, and they sent the coat to their father Jacob by the hand of Naphtali, and they commanded him to say these words:* (Jasher 43:13). Jubilees folds the whole betrayal into two breaths: the plot to kill him, the change of heart, the sale to the Ishmaelites, the house of Potiphar, and then the kid slaughtered and the coat dipped in its blood and sent to Jacob. Jasher opens that second moment wider, the coat torn, the blood of the kid, the coat trampled in the dust and carried to their father by the hand of Naphtali with words the brothers put in his mouth. Both witnesses agree on the order: the sale came first, and the blood on the coat was a lie told afterward to cover it. Jubilees even dates the lie, the tenth of the seventh month, and goes on to say that this is why Yashar'el (Israel) afflicts itself on that day each year; the day a kid's blood was sent to deceive a father became the day of atonement.
cards.s_text: And they hastened and took Joseph’s coat and tore it, and they killed a kid of the goats and dipped the coat in the blood of the kid, and then trampled it in the dust, and they sent the coat to their father Jacob by the hand of Naphtali, and they commanded him to say these words:
cards.t_text: And they dealt treacherously with him, and formed a plot against him to slay him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, priest of the city of ’Êlêw.

cards.note: *And the Egyptian saw the garment of Joseph and the broken door, and heard the words of his wife, and cast Joseph into prison into the place where the prisoners were kept whom the king imprisoned. And he was there in the prison; and Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour in the sight of the chief of the prison guards and compassion before him, for he saw that Yahuah (God) was with him, and that Yahuah (God) made all that he did to prosper.* (Jubilees 39:11–12). *And Potiphar heard their words, and he placed him in the prison house, the place where the king’s prisoners are confined, and Joseph was in the house of confinement twelve years.* (Jasher 44:76). Both witnesses put Joseph in the same place, not a common jail but the prison where the king's own prisoners were kept, and Jasher adds that he was there twelve years. Jubilees adds what Jasher's one line does not, that Yahuah (God) was with him inside the prison, giving him favour with the chief of the guards and prospering everything he did. A master's anger chose the place, yet it was the one prison where Pharaoh's butler and baker would be sent, the only prison from which a road ran to the throne. Twelve years is a long time to be favoured in a cell, but the favour inside the walls was the same favour that would open them.
cards.s_text: And Potiphar heard their words, and he placed him in the prison house, the place where the king’s prisoners are confined, and Joseph was in the house of confinement twelve years.
cards.t_text: And the Egyptian saw the garment of Joseph and the broken door, and heard the words of his wife, and cast Joseph into prison into the place where the prisoners were kept whom the king imprisoned.

cards.note: Jubilees 39:9 — *But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence.* The live Jubilees text holds the same garment-in-her-hands flight as Jasher 44:54.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was afraid of her at her doing this thing, and he rose up to flee from her, and she seized the front of his garments, and in the terror of his flight the garment which Zelicah seized was torn, and Joseph left the garment in the hand of Zelicah, and he fled and got out, for he was in fear.
cards.t_text: But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence.

cards.note: *But he did not surrender his soul, and he remembered Yahuah (God) and the words which Jacob, his father, used to read from amongst the words of Abraham, that no man should commit fornication with a woman who has a husband; that for him the punishment of death has been ordained in the heavens before the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), and the sin will be recorded against him in the eternal books continually before Yahuah (God). And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.* (Jubilees 39:6–7). *And Joseph answered her, saying, It is better for me to remain in this house than to hearken to your words, to sin against Elohim; and she said to him, If you will not perform my wish, I will pluck out your eyes, add fetters to your feet, and will deliver you into the hands of them whom you did not know before.* (Jasher 44:78). Joseph's refusal did not come out of nowhere. Jubilees says he remembered the words of Abraham that his father Jacob used to read aloud, that a man who takes another man's wife has a death sentence written against him in heaven and a sin recorded in the eternal books, and because he remembered he refused. Jasher gives the same refusal in Joseph's own mouth, that he would rather stay in the house than sin against Elohim (God), and it cost him the threat of his eyes and fetters. Adultery was sin in Egypt long before there was a mountain called Sinai, because the commandment was older than the stone it was later written on. Joseph kept Torah because his fathers had kept it and read it to him.
cards.s_text: And Joseph answered her, saying, It is better for me to remain in this house than to hearken to your words, to sin against Elohim; and she said to him, If you will not perform my wish, I will pluck out your eyes, add fetters to your feet, and will deliver you into the hands of them whom you did not know before.
cards.t_text: But he did not surrender his soul, and he remembered Yahuah (God) and the words which Jacob, his father, used to read from amongst the words of Abraham, that no man should commit fornication with a woman who has a husband; that for him the punishment of death has been ordained in the heavens before the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), and the sin will be recorded against him in the eternal books continually before Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *And he set Joseph over all his house, and the blessing of Yahuah (God) came upon the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph, and Yahuah (God) prospered him in all that he did.* (Jubilees 39:3). *And Potiphar took Joseph and brought him to his house that he might serve him, and Joseph found favor in the sight of Potiphar, and he placed confidence in him, and made him overseer over his house, and all that belonged to him he delivered over into his hand.* (Jasher 44:11). Jasher tells how Joseph came into Potiphar's house and found favour there until he was made overseer and everything was put in his hand. Jubilees tells what that meant for the house: the blessing of Yahuah (God) came upon the Egyptian's household on Joseph's account, and everything Potiphar did prospered. A slave sold out of Canaan carried the blessing of Abraham's house into a stranger's house, which is the promise to Abraham working in miniature, that in his seed the families of the earth would be blessed. Potiphar was blessed for the sake of the man he owned.
cards.s_text: And Potiphar took Joseph and brought him to his house that he might serve him, and Joseph found favor in the sight of Potiphar, and he placed confidence in him, and made him overseer over his house, and all that belonged to him he delivered over into his hand.
cards.t_text: And he set Joseph over all his house, and the blessing of Yahuah (God) came upon the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph, and Yahuah (God) prospered him in all that he did.

cards.note: *And Yahudah (Judah) acknowledged, and said: “Tamar is more righteous than I am. And therefore let them burn her not.”* (Jubilees 41:19). *And Tamar rose up and put off the garments of her widowhood, and she put a vail upon her, and she entirely covered herself, and she went and sat in the public thoroughfare, which is upon the road to Timnah.* (Jasher 45:31). These two verses are the beginning and the end of one story. Jasher shows Tamar putting off her widow's garments, veiling herself and sitting on the road to Timnah; Jubilees shows Yahudah (Judah) at the end of it, confessing that she is more righteous than he and refusing to let her be burned. She was not on that road for harlotry. The seed of her dead husband's house was owed to her, Yahudah (Judah) had withheld Shelah, and she went and claimed what Torah gave her by the only door left open. When he saw the pledge he owned it, and the line that runs to Messiah (Christ) passes through the son she bore him.
cards.s_text: And Tamar rose up and put off the garments of her widowhood, and she put a vail upon her, and she entirely covered herself, and she went and sat in the public thoroughfare, which is upon the road to Timnah.
cards.t_text: And Yahudah (Judah) acknowledged, and said: “Tamar is more righteous than I am. And therefore let them burn her not.”

cards.note: *And Onan knew that the seed would not be his, (but) his brother’s only, and he went into the house of his brother’s wife, and spilt the seed on the ground, and he was wicked in the eyes of Yahuah (God), and He slew him.* (Jubilees 41:5). *And Onan took Tamar for a wife and he came to her, and Onan also did like to the work of his brother, and his work was evil in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he slew him also.* (Jasher 45:26). Both witnesses say the same thing in almost the same words: Onan's work was evil in the eyes of Yahuah (God), and He slew him. Jubilees tells why it was evil. Onan knew the seed would not be counted his but his dead brother's, and he spilled it on the ground rather than raise a name for his brother. Jasher adds only that he did as his brother had done, which is to say the house of Yahudah (Judah) lost two sons to the same refusal. The judgment did not fall on lust; it fell on a man who took his brother's wife and would not give his brother a seed.
cards.s_text: And Onan took Tamar for a wife and he came to her, and Onan also did like to the work of his brother, and his work was evil in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he slew him also.
cards.t_text: And Onan knew that the seed would not be his, (but) his brother’s only, and he went into the house of his brother’s wife, and spilt the seed on the ground, and he was wicked in the eyes of Yahuah (God), and He slew him.

cards.note: Jubilees 39:15 — *And the chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them; and he served before them.* Jubilees gives the same prison-attendant setting Jasher 46:6 places Joseph in among the two officers.
cards.s_text: And at the end of the year, they both dreamed dreams in one night, in the place of confinement where they were, and in the morning Joseph came to them to attend upon them as usual, and he saw them, and behold their countenances were dejected and sad.
cards.t_text: And the chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them; and he served before them.

cards.note: Jubilees 39:7 — *And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.* Jubilees records the refusal that made the wife's accusation false, the 'false' charge Joseph names in Jasher 46:11.
cards.s_text: And also that which was told you concerning my master’s wife is false, for they placed me in this dungeon for naught; and the butler answered Joseph, saying, If the king deal well with me as at first, as you last interpreted to me, I will do all that you desire, and get you brought out of this dungeon.
cards.t_text: And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.

cards.note: Jubilees 39:18 — *But the chief butler forgot Joseph in the prison, although he had informed him what would befall him, and did not remember to inform Pharaoh how Joseph had told him for he forgot.* Jubilees tells the same forgetting Jasher 46:19 attributes to Yahuah's hand.
cards.s_text: And the butler, to whom Joseph had interpreted his dream, forgot Joseph, and he did not mention him to the king as he had promised, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) in order to punish Joseph because he had trusted in man.
cards.t_text: But the chief butler forgot Joseph in the prison, although he had informed him what would befall him, and did not remember to inform Pharaoh how Joseph had told him for he forgot.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:11–12 — *I say and testify to you, my sons, according to the judgment which will come upon the man who wishes to injure his brother." And he divided all his possessions between the two on that day, and he gave the larger portion to him that was the first-born, and the tower and all that was about it, and all that Abraham possessed at the Well of the Oath.* Jubilees has Isaac himself divide the estate between the brothers, the same partition Jacob and Esau settle in Jasher 47:15-19.
cards.s_text: If you desire the whole land take it for you and your children forever, and I will take this riches, and it you desire the riches take it to you, and I will take this land for me and for my children to inherit it forever.
cards.t_text: And he divided all his possessions between the two on that day, and he gave the larger portion to him that was the first-born, and the tower and all that was about it, and all that Abraham possessed at the Well of the Oath.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:2 — *Wherefore bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham purchased a sepulchre to bury in; in the sepulchre which I digged for myself, there bury me.* Isaac's request to be laid in Abraham's purchased cave matches the Machpelah burial of Jasher 47:9-10.
cards.s_text: And when Isaac had finished commanding Jacob and his children, he gave up the ghost and died, and was gathered to his people.
cards.t_text: Wherefore bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham purchased a sepulchre to bury in; in the sepulchre which I digged for myself, there bury me.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:18 — *And Isaac slept on his bed that day rejoicing; and he slept the eternal sleep, and died one hundred and eighty years old. He completed twenty-five weeks and five years; and his two sons Esau and Jacob buried him.* Jubilees gives the same death at one hundred and eighty years, buried by Esau and Jacob, that Jasher 47:9 narrates.
cards.s_text: And when Isaac had finished commanding Jacob and his children, he gave up the ghost and died, and was gathered to his people.
cards.t_text: And Isaac slept on his bed that day rejoicing; and he slept the eternal sleep, and died one hundred and eighty years old. He completed twenty-five weeks and five years; and his two sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:3 — *And this I command you, my sons, that you practise righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that Yahuah (God) may bring upon you all that Yahuah (God) said that he would do to Abraham and to his seed.* Jubilees gives the same dying charge to walk in righteousness so the promise to Abraham's seed may come, paralleling Jasher 47:8.
cards.s_text: Now therefore my son, teach your children and your children’s children to fear Yahuah (the Lord), and to go in the good way which will please Yahuah your Elohim (the Lord your God), for if you keep the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) and his statutes Yahuah (the Lord) will also keep to you his covenant with Abraham, and will do well with you and your seed all the days.
cards.t_text: And this I command you, my sons, that you practise righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that Yahuah (God) may bring upon you all that Yahuah (God) said that he would do to Abraham and to his seed.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:6 — *Remember you, my sons, Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham your father, and how I too worshipped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, that He might multiply you and increase your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude, and establish you on the earth as the plant of righteousness which will not be rooted out to all the generations for ever.* Jubilees keeps the same deathbed scene of Isaac invoking the star-seed that Jasher 47:5 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Isaac placed his hands upon all the sons of Jacob, and he took hold of them and embraced them, and kissed them one by one, and Isaac blessed them on that day, and he said to them, May the Elohim (God) of your fathers bless you and increase your seed like the stars of heaven for number.
cards.t_text: Remember you, my sons, Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham your father, and how I too worshipped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, that He might multiply you and increase your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude, and establish you on the earth as the plant of righteousness which will not be rooted out to all the generations for ever.

cards.note: *And he said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were one, and he said to him: “Seven years will come (in which there will be) plenty over all the land of Egypt, and after that seven years of famine, such a famine as has not been in all the land.* (Jubilees 40:3). *Behold the seven years that are coming there will be a great plenty throughout the land, and after that the seven years of famine will follow them, a very grievous famine; and all the plenty will be forgotten from the land, and the famine will consume the inhabitants of the land.* (Jasher 48:55). Joseph gave Pharaoh one reading for two dreams, and both witnesses carry the same reading word for word: seven years of plenty over the land, and after them seven years of famine such as had never been. Jasher's telling adds what the famine would do, that all the plenty would be forgotten and the famine would eat the inhabitants of the land. Jubilees says the two dreams were one, which is why the king needed a Hebrew and not a magician; the doubling was not two messages but one message fixed. The plenty was given so that the famine could be survived, and only one man in Egypt could see that.
cards.s_text: Behold the seven years that are coming there will be a great plenty throughout the land, and after that the seven years of famine will follow them, a very grievous famine; and all the plenty will be forgotten from the land, and the famine will consume the inhabitants of the land.
cards.t_text: And he said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were one, and he said to him: “Seven years will come (in which there will be) plenty over all the land of Egypt, and after that seven years of famine, such a famine as has not been in all the land.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”* (Jubilees 40:5). *And Joseph was then clothed with the spirit of Elohim before the king, and he knew all the things that would befall the king from that day forward, and he knew the proper interpretation of the king’s dream, and he spoke before the king.* (Jasher 48:52). Jasher shows the inside of the thing, Joseph clothed with the spirit of Elohim (God) before the king and knowing what would befall him from that day forward. Jubilees shows the outside, Pharaoh turning to his servants and saying out loud that the spirit of Yahuah (God) was with this man. A heathen king confessed what the court magicians could not produce. The wisdom was not Joseph's own, and Pharaoh knew it, which is why he did not look for a wiser Egyptian; there was none to find.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was then clothed with the spirit of Elohim before the king, and he knew all the things that would befall the king from that day forward, and he knew the proper interpretation of the king’s dream, and he spoke before the king.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”

cards.note: *And then the chief butler remembered Joseph and spake of him to the king, and he brought him forth from the prison, and he told his two dreams before him.* (Jubilees 40:2). *And there was with us a Hebrew servant belonging to the captain of the guard, his name was Joseph, for his master had been angry with him and placed him in the house of confinement, and he attended us there.* (Jasher 48:33). Jubilees gives the hinge in one verse, the chief butler remembering Joseph and speaking of him to the king, and Joseph brought up out of the prison. Jasher gives the butler's actual words, a Hebrew servant of the captain of the guard, put in the house of confinement by an angry master, who attended us there. The man who brought Joseph before Pharaoh was a man Joseph had served in a cell. The service he gave in confinement was the road that carried him out of it, and the one who had forgotten him was the one Yahuah (God) used to remember him.
cards.s_text: And there was with us a Hebrew servant belonging to the captain of the guard, his name was Joseph, for his master had been angry with him and placed him in the house of confinement, and he attended us there.
cards.t_text: And then the chief butler remembered Joseph and spake of him to the king, and he brought him forth from the prison, and he told his two dreams before him.

cards.note: *And in those days Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night concerning a famine which was to be in all the land, and he awoke from his sleep and called all the interpreters of dreams that were in Egypt, and magicians, and told them his two dreams, and they were not able to declare (them).* (Jubilees 40:1). *At that time Pharaoh king of Egypt was sitting upon his throne in the land of Egypt, and lay in his bed and dreamed dreams, and Pharaoh saw in his dream that he was standing by the side of the river of Egypt.* (Jasher 48:2). Jasher sets the scene, Pharaoh on his bed in the land of Egypt, dreaming that he stood by the river. Jubilees tells what the dreams were about and what came of them: two dreams in one night concerning a famine, and all the interpreters and magicians of Egypt called in and unable to say what they meant. Yahuah (God) spoke to a heathen king in his sleep and shut the meaning from every wise man in his court, so that the only door left open was a Hebrew slave in the king's prison. The famine was coming either way; the dream was mercy, and the silence of the magicians was the thing that got Joseph out.
cards.s_text: At that time Pharaoh king of Egypt was sitting upon his throne in the land of Egypt, and lay in his bed and dreamed dreams, and Pharaoh saw in his dream that he was standing by the side of the river of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And in those days Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night concerning a famine which was to be in all the land, and he awoke from his sleep and called all the interpreters of dreams that were in Egypt, and magicians, and told them his two dreams, and they were not able to declare (them).

cards.note: *And the king called Joseph’s name Sĕphânṭîphâns, and gave Joseph to wife the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the chief cook.* (Jubilees 40:10). *And your name no more shall be called Joseph, but Zaphnath Paaneah shall be your name; you shall be second to me, and according to your word shall be all the affairs of my government, and at your word shall my people go out and come in.* (Jasher 49:21). The king gives Joseph a new name, and both books record it. Jubilees writes it as Sĕphânṭîphâns and Jasher writes it as Zaphnath Paaneah; it is one Egyptian name heard through two scribes' ears, the same name Genesis carries. Jasher adds what the name meant in Pharaoh's mouth: second to me, every affair of the government at your word, the people going out and coming in at your word. Jubilees adds the wife, the priest's daughter from Heliopolis. The two books do not compete; each keeps a piece of the same afternoon in Pharaoh's court.
cards.s_text: And your name no more shall be called Joseph, but Zaphnath Paaneah shall be your name; you shall be second to me, and according to your word shall be all the affairs of my government, and at your word shall my people go out and come in.
cards.t_text: And the king called Joseph’s name Sĕphânṭîphâns, and gave Joseph to wife the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the chief cook.

cards.note: Jubilees 40:8 — *And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.* Jubilees gives the righteous character of the second-to-Pharaoh that Jasher 49:22 establishes.
cards.s_text: Also from under your hand shall my servants and officers receive their salary which is given to them monthly, and to you shall all the people of the land bow down; only in my throne will I be greater than you.
cards.t_text: And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.

cards.note: Jubilees 40:5 — *And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”* Jubilees narrates the identical Pharaoh-speech that opens Jasher 49:8.
cards.s_text: And the king said to all the officers: I have thought that since Elohim (God) has made known to the Hebrew man all that he has spoken, there is none so discreet and wise in the whole land as he is; if it seem good in your sight I will place him over the land, for he will save the land with his wisdom.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”

cards.note: *And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.* (Jubilees 40:8). *And at the revolution of the year, in the second year of Joseph’s reigning over Egypt, Yahuah (the Lord) gave great plenty throughout the land for seven years as Joseph had spoken, for Yahuah (the Lord) blessed all the produce of the earth in those days for seven years, and they ate and were greatly satisfied.* (Jasher 50:7). Jasher tells of the second year of Joseph's reign, when Yahuah (the Lord) gave the great plenty for seven years exactly as Joseph had spoken. Jubilees tells what kind of man was reigning while the plenty came: one who walked in uprightness, without pride, with no respect of persons, who took no gifts and judged all the people of the land fairly. That is the judge Torah later requires of Yashar'el (Israel), and here he is, a Hebrew ruling Egypt. The land was fed under a ruler who could not be bought, and the princes and servants loved him for it.
cards.s_text: And at the revolution of the year, in the second year of Joseph’s reigning over Egypt, Yahuah (the Lord) gave great plenty throughout the land for seven years as Joseph had spoken, for Yahuah (the Lord) blessed all the produce of the earth in those days for seven years, and they ate and were greatly satisfied.
cards.t_text: And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:6–7 — *And after that he set them free again, and detained Simeon alone and sent off his nine brothers. And he filled their sacks with corn, and he put their gold in their sacks, and they did not know.* The live Jubilees layer keeps Simeon detained and the gold secretly restored, as Jasher 51:37-45.
cards.s_text: And Joseph went out from them and came into the chamber, and wept a great weeping, for his pity was excited for them, and he washed his face, and returned to them again, and he took Simeon from them and ordered him to be bound, but Simeon was not willing to be done so, for he was a very powerful man and they could not bind him.
cards.t_text: And after that he set them free again, and detained Simeon alone and sent off his nine brothers.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:5 — *And Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him, and he spake to them and questioned them, and he said to them: “Are you not spies, and have you not come to explore the approaches of the land?” And he put them in ward.* The live Jubilees layer carries the same recognition and spy-charge as Jasher 51:20-24.
cards.s_text: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but they knew him not, for Joseph was very great in their eyes, therefore they knew him not.
cards.t_text: And Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him, and he spake to them and questioned them, and he said to them: “Are you not spies, and have you not come to explore the approaches of the land?” And he put them in ward.

cards.note: *(Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)* (Jubilees 42:4). *And Jacob afterward heard that there was corn in Egypt, and he called to his sons to go to Egypt to buy corn, for upon them also did the famine prevail, and he called to his sons, saying,* (Jasher 51:1). Both witnesses put the same scene at the door of the reunion: Jacob hearing that there is food in Egypt and sending his sons down to buy it, because the famine had reached Canaan too. Jubilees adds the detail the whole testing turns on, that he sent ten and kept Benjamin home. The famine that drove the ten down was the same famine Joseph had been set over, so the sons of Jacob were walking toward the brother they had sold without knowing it. Benjamin being withheld is what gave Joseph the lever he would use to find out whether they had changed.
cards.s_text: And Jacob afterward heard that there was corn in Egypt, and he called to his sons to go to Egypt to buy corn, for upon them also did the famine prevail, and he called to his sons, saying,
cards.t_text: (Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)

cards.note: Jubilees 42:4 — *(Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)* Jubilees opens the same famine and sending that drives Jasher 52:7.
cards.s_text: And in those days the famine was sore throughout the land, and all the people of the earth went and came to Egypt to buy food, for the famine prevailed greatly amongst them, and the sons of Jacob remained in Canaan a year and two months until their corn was finished.
cards.t_text: (Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)

cards.note: Jubilees 42:18 — *And Reuben said: “Give him into my hand, and if I do not bring him back to you, slay my two sons instead of his soul.” And he said to him He will not go with you."* Jubilees likewise records the firstborn's rejected surety before Judah's, matching Jasher 52:5.
cards.s_text: And Reuben said to his father, You shall slay my two sons if I do not bring your son and place him before you; and Jacob said to his sons, Abide you here and do not go down to Egypt, for my son shall not go down with you to Egypt, nor die like his brother.
cards.t_text: And Reuben said: “Give him into my hand, and if I do not bring him back to you, slay my two sons instead of his soul.” And he said to him He will not go with you."

cards.note: Jubilees 43:13 — *Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever.* Jubilees carries Judah's surety to its climax — offering himself a bondsman — the same pledge first given in Jasher 52:19.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to Jacob his father, Give the lad into my care and we will rise up and go down to Egypt and buy corn, and then return, and it shall be when we return if the lad be not with us, then let me bear your blame forever.
cards.t_text: Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."

cards.note: Jubilees 42:11–12 — *And he said: “My son will not go down with you lest perchance he fall sick; for their mother gave birth to two sons, and one has perished, and this one also you will take from me. If perchance he took a fever on the road, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to death.” For he saw that their money had been returned to every man in his sack, and for this reason he feared to send him.* Jasher 52:4 carries Jacob's same fear of losing the last son of Rachel.
cards.s_text: Now therefore my son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead and he is left alone, and mischief may befall him by the way in which you go, as it befell his brother.
cards.t_text: And he said: “My son will not go down with you lest perchance he fall sick; for their mother gave birth to two sons, and one has perished, and this one also you will take from me. If perchance he took a fever on the road, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to death.”

cards.note: Jubilees 42:10 — *And Jacob said: “Me have you bereaved of my children! Joseph is not and Simeon also is not, and you will take Benjamin away. On me has your wickedness come.”* Jubilees records the same grieving father at the same moment as Jasher 52:5.
cards.s_text: And Reuben said to his father, You shall slay my two sons if I do not bring your son and place him before you; and Jacob said to his sons, Abide you here and do not go down to Egypt, for my son shall not go down with you to Egypt, nor die like his brother.
