cards.t_text: And Jacob said: “Me have you bereaved of my children! Joseph is not and Simeon also is not, and you will take Benjamin away. On me has your wickedness come.”

cards.note: Jubilees 43:13 — *Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever.* Jubilees keeps Judah's surety-plea that Jasher 53:31 begins, the same intercession before Joseph.
cards.s_text: And Judah said, What shall we say to our Lord, what shall we speak and how shall we justify ourselves, Elohim has this day found the iniquity of all your servants, therefore has he done this thing to us this day.
cards.t_text: Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."

cards.note: Jubilees 43:1 — *And he did as Joseph had told him, and filled all their sacks for them with food and put their money in their sacks, and put the cup in Benjamin’s sack.* Jubilees narrates the same hidden cup that Jasher 53:23 sets in Benjamin's sack.
cards.s_text: At that time Joseph commanded his officer to fill their sacks with food, and to put each man’s money into his sack, and to put the cup in the sack of Benjamin, and to give them provision for the road, and they did so to them.
cards.t_text: And he did as Joseph had told him, and filled all their sacks for them with food and put their money in their sacks, and put the cup in Benjamin’s sack.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:23 — *And they ate before him and he gave them all a portion, but the portion of Benjamin was seven times larger than that of any of theirs.* Jubilees, like Jasher 53:14, marks Benjamin's portion as far greater than his brothers' at Joseph's table.
cards.s_text: And Benjamin went up before Joseph and sat upon the throne, and the men beheld the acts of Joseph, and they were astonished at them; and the men ate and drank at that time with Joseph, and he then gave presents to them, and Joseph gave one gift to Benjamin, and Manasseh and Ephraim saw the acts of their father, and they also gave presents to him, and Osnath gave him one present, and they were five presents in the hand of Benjamin.
cards.t_text: And they ate before him and he gave them all a portion, but the portion of Benjamin was seven times larger than that of any of theirs.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:21 — *And they went and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother, and he knew him, and said to them: “Is this your youngest brother?” And they said to him: “It is he.” And he said: “Yahuah (God) be gracious to you, my son!”* Jubilees narrates the same arrival with Benjamin that Jasher 53:1 opens, the parallel patriarchal record.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob rose up and took Benjamin and the whole of the presents, and they went and came to Egypt and they stood before Joseph.
cards.t_text: And they went and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother, and he knew him, and said to them: “Is this your youngest brother?” And they said to him: “It is he.” And he said: “Yahuah (God) be gracious to you, my son!”

cards.note: *And Joseph saw that they were all accordant in goodness one with another, and he could not refrain himself, and he told them that he was Joseph.* (Jubilees 43:14). *And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.* (Jasher 54:69). Jubilees tells exactly when Joseph broke: when he saw that his brothers were all of one accord in goodness toward one another, he could not hold himself and told them who he was. Jasher gives the words, I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, and the comfort that came with them, that Elohim (God) had sent him ahead of them to keep them alive through the famine. He did not reveal himself to the men who had sold him; he waited until he saw them stand together for Benjamin, which was the opposite of what they had done to him. The test was whether they had changed, and when they had, the hidden brother showed his face.
cards.s_text: And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.
cards.t_text: And Joseph saw that they were all accordant in goodness one with another, and he could not refrain himself, and he told them that he was Joseph.

cards.note: *Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."* (Jubilees 43:13). *And Judah answered Joseph, saying, Surely you must know that I was security for the lad to his father, saying, If I brought him not to him I should bear his blame forever.* (Jasher 54:57). Jasher and Jubilees carry Yahudah's (Judah's) plea almost word for word: he had become surety for the lad to his father, and if he did not bring him back he would bear the blame for ever. Jubilees adds the offer that goes with it, let me stay as a bondsman in the boy's place and let the lad go home with his brothers. The brother who once proposed selling Joseph now offers himself as a slave so that Rachel's other son can go free. That is the change Joseph was waiting to see, and it is why the next thing in the story is Joseph weeping and telling them who he is.
cards.s_text: And Judah answered Joseph, saying, Surely you must know that I was security for the lad to his father, saying, If I brought him not to him I should bear his blame forever.
cards.t_text: Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."

cards.note: Jubilees 45:11–12 — *And this was the first year of the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee. And Joseph took of the corn of the harvest the fifth part for the king and left four parts for them for food and for seed, and Joseph made it an ordinance for the land of Egypt until this day.* Jubilees keeps the same fifth-part ordinance behind Joseph's gathering in Jasher 55:30.
cards.s_text: And Joseph purchased all the lands and fields of Egypt for bread on the account of Pharaoh, and Joseph supplied all Egypt with bread all the days of the famine, and Joseph collected all the silver and gold that came to him for the corn which they bought throughout the land, and he accumulated much gold and silver, besides an immense quantity of onyx stones, bdellium and valuable garments which they brought to Joseph from every part of the land when their money was spent.
cards.t_text: And Joseph took of the corn of the harvest the fifth part for the king and left four parts for them for food and for seed, and Joseph made it an ordinance for the land of Egypt until this day.

cards.note: Jubilees 45:6–7 — *And Joseph had given to his father and to his brothers as a gift the right of dwelling in the land of Goshen and in Rameses and all the region round about, which he ruled over before Pharaoh. And Yashar'el (Israel) and his sons dwelt in the land of Goshen, the best part of the land of Egypt; and Yashar'el (Israel) was one hundred and thirty years old when he came into Egypt, And Joseph nourished his father and his brethren and also their possessions with bread as much as sufficed them for the seven years of the famine.* Jubilees carries the same Goshen grant and the same hundred-and-thirtieth year Jasher 55:26 records.
cards.s_text: In the second year, that is in the hundred and thirtieth year of the life of Jacob, Joseph maintained his father and his brethren, and all his father’s household, with bread according to their little ones, all the days of the famine; they lacked nothing.
cards.t_text: And Joseph had given to his father and to his brothers as a gift the right of dwelling in the land of Goshen and in Rameses and all the region round about, which he ruled over before Pharaoh. And Yashar’el (Israel) and his sons dwelt in the land of Goshen, the best part of the land of Egypt; and Yashar’el (Israel) was one hundred and thirty years old when he came into Egypt,

cards.note: Jubilees 45:1 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* Jubilees dates the same going-out-from-Canaan that Jasher 55:5 narrates from Beersheba into Goshen.
cards.s_text: At that time Jacob commanded his sons and household to go to Egypt according to the word of Yahuah (the Lord) to him, and Jacob rose up with his sons and all his household, and he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart, and they went to the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Yashar’el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

cards.note: Jubilees 45:13 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and all the days which he lived were three jubilees, one hundred and forty-seven years, and he died in the fourth year of the fifth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* Jubilees keeps the same seventeen years and 147-year total that frames Jasher 56:1, with the deathbed blessing of the sons.
cards.s_text: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, and the years of his life were a hundred and forty seven years.
cards.t_text: And Yashar’el (Israel) lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and all the days which he lived were three jubilees, one hundred and forty-seven years, and he died in the fourth year of the fifth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:6 — *And he made them swear regarding his bones, for he knew that the Egyptians would not again bring forth and bury him in the land of Canaan...* The latter-day troubles and visitation Jacob foretells in Jasher 56:20 are framed in Jubilees by Joseph's sworn oath over his bones as the affliction nears.
cards.s_text: For I know that many and grievous troubles will befall you in the latter days in the land, yea your children and children’s children, only serve Yahuah (the Lord) and he will save you from all trouble.
cards.t_text: And he made them swear regarding his bones, for he knew that the Egyptians would not again bring forth and bury him in the land of Canaan, for Mâkamârôn, king of Canaan, while dwelling in the land of Assyria, fought in the valley with the king of Egypt and slew him there, and pursued after the Egyptians to the gates of ’Êrmôn.

cards.note: Jubilees 38:14–15 — *And the sons of Edom have not got quit of the yoke of servitude which the twelve sons of Jacob had imposed on them until this day. And these are the kings that reigned in Edom before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar’el (Israel) until this day in the land of Edom.* Jasher 57:40's vow to take a king 'from a strange land to this day' frames the same Edomite king-list Jubilees opens here.
cards.s_text: Therefore the sons of Esau swore, saying, From that day forward they would not choose a king from their brethren, but one from a strange land to this day.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Edom have not got quit of the yoke of servitude which the twelve sons of Jacob had imposed on them until this day.

cards.note: *And Bâlâq, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Danâbâ.* (Jubilees 38:16). *And all the children of Esau took him and anointed him and they crowned him for a king, and they bowed down to him, and they said to him, May the king live, may the king live.* (Jasher 57:42). Jubilees gives the name and the city, Balaq the son of Beor reigning in Edom from Danaba. Jasher shows the crowning itself, the children of Esau anointing a king and bowing to him and shouting that the king should live. Edom had a throne and a shout of loyalty while the sons of Jacob were still a family of shepherds, and long before Yashar'el (Israel) asked for a king of its own. The elder brother built a kingdom first; it did not make him the heir.
cards.s_text: And all the children of Esau took him and anointed him and they crowned him for a king, and they bowed down to him, and they said to him, May the king live, may the king live.
cards.t_text: And Bâlâq, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Danâbâ.

cards.note: *And the sons of Jacob pressed hard upon the sons of Esau in the mountains of Seir, and bowed their necks so that they became servants of the sons of Jacob.* (Jubilees 38:10). *And it came to pass after the battle, the children of Esau turned back and came home to Seir, and the children of Esau slew those who had remained in the land of the children of Seir; they slew also their wives and little ones, they left not a soul alive except fifty young lads and damsels whom they suffered to live, and the children of Esau did not put them to death, and the lads became their slaves, and the damsels they took for wives.* (Jasher 57:35). These are two layers of the same mountain. Jubilees shows the sons of Jacob pressing the sons of Esau hard in Seir and bowing their necks until they served Jacob's sons. Jasher shows what the sons of Esau did when they came home from battle to Seir: they slaughtered the Horites who were left, wives and little ones, and kept only fifty lads and damsels, the lads as slaves and the damsels as wives. The ones made servants of Jacob turned and made servants of others, and the land of Seir changed hands by the sword twice over. Esau's house was always strong against the weak and bowed before the brother it hated.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the battle, the children of Esau turned back and came home to Seir, and the children of Esau slew those who had remained in the land of the children of Seir; they slew also their wives and little ones, they left not a soul alive except fifty young lads and damsels whom they suffered to live, and the children of Esau did not put them to death, and the lads became their slaves, and the damsels they took for wives.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Jacob pressed hard upon the sons of Esau in the mountains of Seir, and bowed their necks so that they became servants of the sons of Jacob.

cards.note: *And Simeon and Benjamin and Enoch, Reuben’s son, went forth on the west side of the tower, and fifty (men) with them, and they slew of Edom and of the Horites four hundred men, stout warriors; and six hundred fled, and four of the sons of Esau fled with them, and left their father lying slain, as he had fallen on the hill which is in ’Adûrâm.* (Jubilees 38:8). *And the battle was heavy between them, and the sons of Esau were smitten before the sons of Jacob, and the sons of Jacob slew of the sons of Esau eighty men, and not one died of the people of the sons of Jacob; and the hand of Joseph prevailed over all the people of the sons of Esau, and he took Zepho, the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and fifty of his men captive, and he bound them with chains of iron, and gave them into the hand of his servants to bring them to Egypt.* (Jasher 57:2). Both witnesses tell of the sons of Jacob prevailing over the sons of Esau in the country of Seir, but they are not the same battle. Jubilees tells the one in which Esau himself fell on the hill at Aduram, Simeon and Benjamin and Reuben's son Enoch going out from the west side of the tower and slaying four hundred of Edom and the Horites. Jasher tells the later war, when Joseph's hand prevailed, eighty of Esau's sons fell and not one of Jacob's, and Zepho was taken in iron chains to Egypt. The feud did not end with Esau's death; his grandchildren came back for more and were beaten again. The enmity between the two brothers' houses outlived both brothers.
cards.s_text: And the battle was heavy between them, and the sons of Esau were smitten before the sons of Jacob, and the sons of Jacob slew of the sons of Esau eighty men, and not one died of the people of the sons of Jacob; and the hand of Joseph prevailed over all the people of the sons of Esau, and he took Zepho, the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and fifty of his men captive, and he bound them with chains of iron, and gave them into the hand of his servants to bring them to Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Simeon and Benjamin and Enoch, Reuben’s son, went forth on the west side of the tower, and fifty (men) with them, and they slew of Edom and of the Horites four hundred men, stout warriors; and six hundred fled, and four of the sons of Esau fled with them, and left their father lying slain, as he had fallen on the hill which is in ’Adûrâm.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:1 — *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* Jubilees tells the same multiplying-and-secure years of Jasher 58:13 — the seed growing into a nation while Joseph lives.
cards.s_text: And also all his brethren the sons of Jacob dwelt securely in the land, all the days of Joseph, and they were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly in the land, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, as their father Jacob had commanded them.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:14 — *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* Jubilees opens the same Egyptian affliction that begins in Jasher 59:28.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Joseph, all the Egyptians began in those days to rule over the children of Israel, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who reigned in his father’s stead, took all the laws of Egypt and conducted the whole government of Egypt under his counsel, and he reigned securely over his people.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:3 — *And Joseph died being a hundred and ten years old; seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt.* Jubilees gives the same hundred-and-ten-year reckoning of Joseph's life that Jasher 59:26 records at his death.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was one hundred and ten years old when he died in the land of Egypt, and all his brethren and all his servants rose up and they embalmed Joseph, as was their custom, and his brethren and all Egypt mourned over him for seventy days.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died being a hundred and ten years old; seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:5 — *And he commanded the children of Yashar'el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.* Jubilees records the very bones-charge Joseph swears the seed to in Jasher 59:24.
cards.s_text: And Joseph made the sons of Israel to swear for their seed after them, saying, Elohim will surely visit you and you shall bring up my bones with you from here.
cards.t_text: And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:3 — *And Joseph died being a hundred and ten years old; seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt.* Jasher and Jubilees both reckon "after the death of Joseph," agreeing with Genesis on his hundred and ten years.
cards.s_text: And when the year came round, being the seventy-second year from the Israelites going down to Egypt, after the death of Joseph, Zepho, the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, fled from Egypt, he and his men, and they went away.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died being a hundred and ten years old; seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:1 — *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar'el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* Jubilees narrates the very years Jasher dates by, the seed multiplying in Egypt after Joseph — the same window from a parallel hand.
cards.s_text: And when the year came round, being the seventy-second year from the Israelites going down to Egypt, after the death of Joseph, Zepho, the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, fled from Egypt, he and his men, and they went away.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:4 — *And he died and all his brethren and all that generation.* Jubilees seals the dying generation in the same words, beside which Jasher's death-roll of Jacob's sons (61:3-4) takes its place. It ain't new.
cards.s_text: And in the seventy-fifth year died his brother Simeon, he was a hundred and twenty years old at his death, and he was also put into a coffin and given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And he died and all his brethren and all that generation.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:14 — *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* Jubilees carries the identical scene — Israel pressed to build Pharaoh's cities — confirming Jasher's opening of the bondage. It ain't new.
cards.s_text: And he also commanded the sons of Jacob to assist the Egyptians in the building, and the Egyptians made a beautiful and elegant palace for a royal habitation, and he dwelt in it and he renewed his government and he reigned securely.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* (Jubilees 46:1). *In that year, being the seventy-ninth year of the Israelites going down to Egypt, died Reuben the son of Jacob, in the land of Egypt; Reuben was a hundred and twenty-five years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin, and he was given into the hands of his children.* (Jasher 62:1). Jasher counts this season by funerals, and here it is Reuben, dead at a hundred and twenty-five in the seventy-ninth year of the going down, put into a coffin and left in his children's keeping. Jubilees counts the same season by the living: after Jacob died the children of Yashar'el (Israel) multiplied in Egypt and became a great nation, brother loving brother, for ten weeks of years, all the days of Joseph. The fathers were being laid in coffins one by one while the seed grew into a people in a land that was not theirs. Both things were happening at once, and both had been told to Abram beforehand.
cards.s_text: In that year, being the seventy-ninth year of the Israelites going down to Egypt, died Reuben the son of Jacob, in the land of Egypt; Reuben was a hundred and twenty-five years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin, and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: *And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and his brethren died after him.* (Jubilees 46:8). *And it came to pass at that time that Judah the son of Jacob died in Egypt, in the eighty-sixth year of Jacob’s going down to Egypt, and Judah was a hundred and twenty-nine years old at his death, and they embalmed him and put him into a coffin, and he was given into the hands of his children.* (Jasher 62:23). Jubilees says it in one breath: Joseph died and was buried in Egypt, and his brethren died after him. Jasher spreads that one breath across a roll of dated deaths, and this entry is Yahudah (Judah), a hundred and twenty-nine years old in the eighty-sixth year of the going down, embalmed and put into a coffin and given to his children. The embalming and the coffin were not Egyptian vanity. The fathers were being kept, not buried, because the family knew they were going home and the bones were going with them.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass at that time that Judah the son of Jacob died in Egypt, in the eighty-sixth year of Jacob’s going down to Egypt, and Judah was a hundred and twenty-nine years old at his death, and they embalmed him and put him into a coffin, and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and his brethren died after him.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:5 — *And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.* The same bones-oath that frames the fathers' burials in Jasher 63:1.
cards.s_text: And in the ninety-third year died Levi, the son of Jacob, in Egypt, and Levi was a hundred and thirty-seven years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:13 — *“Behold the people of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.”* The same forgetting-king's counsel to afflict the seed Jasher 63:6 records.
cards.s_text: Therefore all Egypt began from that day forth to embitter the lives of the sons of Jacob, and to afflict them with all manner of hard labor, because they had not known their ancestors who had delivered them in the days of the famine.
cards.t_text: “Behold the people of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.”

cards.note: Jubilees 46:15 — *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* Jubilees tells the same affliction after Joseph's generation passed that Jasher 63:3 records.
cards.s_text: And the hand of all Egypt became more grievous in those days against the children of Israel, and the Egyptians injured the Israelites until the children of Israel were wearied of their lives on account of the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: *And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and his brethren died after him.* (Jubilees 46:8). *For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.* (Jasher 64:8). The death of Joseph and his brethren was not only a grief inside Yashar'el (Israel); it was a signal outside it. Jasher shows Zepho, Esau's grandson, hearing that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren were dead, and that only their children remained, and that is when he moved. Jubilees gives the deaths plainly, Joseph in the forty-sixth jubilee and his brethren after him. Enemies wait for the generation of the fathers to pass before they come against the children, and the king who knew not Joseph was of the same mind as Zepho.
cards.s_text: For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and his brethren died after him.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:15 — *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* Jubilees carries the same paradox of Jasher 65:38 — rigour breeds growth.
cards.s_text: And all the work wherein the Egyptians made the children of Israel labor, they exacted with rigor, in order to afflict the children of Israel, but the more they afflicted them, the more they increased and grew, and the Egyptians were grieved because of the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* (Jubilees 46:14). *Behold in the land are Pithom and Rameses, cities unfortified against battle, it behooves you and us to build them, and to fortify them.* (Jasher 65:8). Jasher records the counsel that proposed the work: Pithom and Rameses stood unfortified against battle, and the Egyptians said it behooved them to build and fortify. Jubilees records the work itself: taskmasters set over the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and the strong cities Pithom and Raamses built for Pharaoh, with all the walls and fortifications that had fallen. The one book gives the plan and the other gives the labour, and the same two cities stand at the centre of both. The fortifying Jasher's counsellors called for is the fortification Jubilees says Yashar'el (Israel) raised with their own hands under the taskmasters.
cards.s_text: Behold in the land are Pithom and Rameses, cities unfortified against battle, it behooves you and us to build them, and to fortify them.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:13 — *“Behold the people of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.”* Jubilees retells the identical council of Jasher 65:3-6.
cards.s_text: Behold the people of the children of Israel is greater and mightier than we are, and you know all the evil which they did to us in the road when we returned from battle.
cards.t_text: “Behold the people of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.”

cards.note: Jubilees 47:2 — *And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.* Jubilees records the same river-decree against the male children that Jasher 66:21 has Job propose.
cards.s_text: If it please the king, let a royal decree go forth, and let it be written in the laws of Egypt which shall not be revoked, that every male child born to the Israelites, his blood shall be spilled upon the ground.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:13 — *"Behold the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan."* Jubilees stages the same royal counsel against Israel that Jasher 66:12-14 dramatizes.
cards.s_text: Now therefore our Lord and king, the eyes of all Egypt are upon you to give them advice with your wisdom, by which they may prevail over Israel to destroy them, or to diminish them from the land; and the king answered them saying, Give you counsel in this matter that we may know what to do to them.
cards.t_text: “Behold the people of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.”

cards.note: Jubilees 46:15 — *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* Jubilees carries the same paradox as Jasher 66:9 — rigour met with multiplication.
cards.s_text: But as the Egyptians increased the labor upon the children of Israel, so did the children of Israel increase and multiply, and all Egypt was filled with the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* (Jubilees 46:15). *And when they ploughed they were unable to hurt the infants of the children of Israel, so the people increased and waxed exceedingly.* (Jasher 67:59). Jubilees gives the rule: the more Egypt dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied. Jasher gives the strangest proof of it, the Egyptians ploughing the ground where the Hebrew women had given birth and finding they could not harm the infants, so the people grew all the more. Rigour, ploughing, and later the river, and every one of them a failure. What was meant to cut off the seed became the thing under which it multiplied, because the one who had promised Abraham a seed like the sand of the sea was the one keeping count.
cards.s_text: And when they ploughed they were unable to hurt the infants of the children of Israel, so the people increased and waxed exceedingly.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: *And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.* (Jubilees 47:2). *If it please the king let him order all their children which shall be born from this day forward, to be thrown into the water, for by this can you wipe away their name, for none of them, nor of their fathers, were tried in this manner.* (Jasher 67:49). Jubilees gives the decree, Pharaoh commanding that every male child born to them be thrown into the river. Jasher gives where the decree came from: Balaam counselling the king to throw the children into the water, and saying the aim out loud, by this you can wipe away their name. The war was never only about numbers; it was against the name of the seed. The same Balaam would later be hired to curse that seed in the wilderness, and here he is already at work before Moses was born. The order came from a prophet for hire before it came from a king.
cards.s_text: If it please the king let him order all their children which shall be born from this day forward, to be thrown into the water, for by this can you wipe away their name, for none of them, nor of their fathers, were tried in this manner.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.

cards.note: Jubilees 47:9 — *And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.* The Jubilees parallel to Jasher 68:24, the grown child made the daughter's son and brought into Pharaoh's court.
cards.s_text: And at the end of two years, when the child grew up, she brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he was to her as a son, and she called his name Moses, for she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
cards.t_text: And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.

cards.note: *And in those days Tharmuth, the daughter of Pharaoh, came to bathe in the river, and she heard your voice crying, and she told her maidens to bring you forth, and they brought you to her.* (Jubilees 47:5). *And Bathia lifted up her eyes to the river, and she saw the ark upon the water, and sent her maid to fetch it.* (Jasher 68:18). Jubilees calls her Tharmuth and Jasher calls her Bathia, but both set the same scene: Pharaoh's daughter at the river, seeing or hearing the child, and sending her maid to bring it up out of the water. The river was the decree; the rescue came out of the very river, and by the hand of Pharaoh's own house. Jubilees tells it to Moses in the second person, she heard your voice crying, because this is the Angel reciting Moses' own life back to him. The king's daughter undid the king's command without knowing it.
cards.s_text: And Bathia lifted up her eyes to the river, and she saw the ark upon the water, and sent her maid to fetch it.
cards.t_text: And in those days Tharmuth, the daughter of Pharaoh, came to bathe in the river, and she heard your voice crying, and she told her maidens to bring you forth, and they brought you to her.

cards.note: Jubilees 47:4 — *And she made an ark for you, and covered it with pitch and asphalt, and placed it in the flags on the bank of the river, and she placed you in it seven days, and your mother came by night and suckled you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds.* The Jubilees ark and watching Miriam set beside Jasher 68:13-14.
cards.s_text: And the woman hastened to take away her son before the officers came, and she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child in it, and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.
cards.t_text: And she made an ark for you, and covered it with pitch and asphalt, and placed it in the flags on the bank of the river, and she placed you in it seven days, and your mother came by night and suckled you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds.

cards.note: Jubilees 47:3 — *And they cast them in for seven months until the day that you were born. And your mother hid you for three months, and they told regarding her.* The Jubilees parallel keeps the same seven-month bondage of casting-in and the three-month hiding behind Jasher 68:5.
cards.s_text: And when the woman saw the child that it was good and pleasing to the sight, she hid it for three months in an inner room.
cards.t_text: And they cast them in for seven months until the day that you were born. And your mother hid you for three months, and they told regarding her.

cards.note: *And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.* (Jubilees 47:2). *And Pharaoh sent his officers to take the children and slay them; thus did the Egyptians to the Hebrew women all the days.* (Jasher 68:11). Jubilees gives the decree; Jasher shows it in force, Pharaoh's officers sent out to take the children and slay them, and the note that this was done to the Hebrew women all the days. The command was not a single bad night. It was a standing order carried out every day, and that is the Egypt Moses was born into. His mother's ark on the water was an answer to a decree that had been running for years, and it had to be hidden because the officers were still coming.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh sent his officers to take the children and slay them; thus did the Egyptians to the Hebrew women all the days.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:14 — *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* Jubilees names the taskmasters and Pharaoh's building-cities behind the long, daily Egyptian labor of Jasher 69:8.
cards.s_text: And the men of Egypt did so to all the children of Israel day by day, all the days for a long period.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:15 — *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* Jubilees gives the same rigorous bondage Jasher 69:5 decrees, with the same paradox — the seed multiplies under the lash.
cards.s_text: Then Pharaoh commanded in those days that a proclamation should be issued throughout Egypt to the children of Israel, saying, No man shall diminish any thing of his daily labor.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:1 — *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar'el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* Jubilees records the same multiplying nation in Egypt that Jasher 69:4 says Pharaoh's counsel could not stop.
cards.s_text: And when Pharaoh king of Egypt saw that the counsel which Balaam had advised respecting the children of Israel did not succeed, but that still they were fruitful, multiplied and increased throughout the land of Egypt,
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: *And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.* (Jubilees 47:9). *And when Moses grew up in the king’s house, Bathia the daughter of Pharaoh considered him as a son, and all the household of Pharaoh honored him, and all the men of Egypt were afraid of him.* (Jasher 70:33). Jasher tells it from the outside: Moses grown in the king's house, Bathia counting him as her son, the household honouring him and all Egypt afraid of him. Jubilees tells it to Moses himself, the Angel reciting his own life back to him in the second person, you became her son, and they brought you into the royal court. But Jubilees keeps one thing Jasher does not: before the court had him, Amram his father taught him writing. The Hebrew father's teaching came first, and then Pharaoh's house. He was raised in the court, but he was taught at home.
cards.s_text: And when Moses grew up in the king’s house, Bathia the daughter of Pharaoh considered him as a son, and all the household of Pharaoh honored him, and all the men of Egypt were afraid of him.
cards.t_text: And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:1 — *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* Jubilees marks the same departure out of Egypt to Midian that Jasher 71:11 narrates.
cards.s_text: And the angel of Yahuah (the Lord) took hold of the right hand of Moses, and brought him forth from Egypt, and placed him from without the borders of Egypt, a distance of forty days’ journey.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: Jubilees 47:11–12 — *And on the second day you did find two of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) striving together, and you did say to him who was doing the wrong: "Why do you smite your brother? And he was angry and indignant, and said “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Thinkest you to kill me as you killedst the Egyptian yesterday?” And you did fear and flee on account of these words.* Jubilees gives the same exchange and the flight that follows Jasher 71:8.
cards.s_text: And he answered him and said to him, Who has set you for a prince and judge over us? dost you think to slay me as you did slay the Egyptian? and Moses was afraid and he said, Surely the thing is known?
cards.t_text: And on the second day you did find two of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) striving together, and you did say to him who was doing the wrong: "Why do you smite your brother?

cards.note: Jubilees 47:10 — *And you were three weeks of years at court until the time when you did go forth from the royal court and did see an Egyptian smiting your friend who was of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and you did slay him and hide him in the sand.* Jubilees carries the identical scene that Jasher 71:1-3 expands.
cards.s_text: And when Moses heard this wicked thing, his anger was kindled against the Egyptian, and he turned this way and the other, and when he saw there was no man there he smote the Egyptian and hid him in the sand, and delivered the Hebrew from the hand of him that smote him.
cards.t_text: And you were three weeks of years at court until the time when you did go forth from the royal court and did see an Egyptian smiting your friend who was of the children of Yashar’el (Israel), and you did slay him and hide him in the sand.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:1 — *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* Jubilees has Moses depart to Midian where Jasher 72:22 has him flee Egypt — the same exile.
cards.s_text: And Moses was eighteen years old when he fled from Egypt from the presence of Pharaoh, and he fled and escaped to the camp of Kikianus, which at that time was besieging Cush.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: *And you were three weeks of years at court until the time when you did go forth from the royal court and did see an Egyptian smiting your friend who was of the children of Yashar’el (Israel), and you did slay him and hide him in the sand.* (Jubilees 47:10). *At that time that the war and the siege were against Cush, Moses fled from Egypt from Pharaoh who sought to kill him for having slain the Egyptian.* (Jasher 72:21). Jubilees gives the deed, told to Moses as his own memory: he went out from the court, saw an Egyptian smiting his friend of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), slew him and hid him in the sand. Jasher gives what followed, Moses fleeing because Pharaoh sought to kill him for it, and sets the flight in the days of the war against Cush. The man raised in the king's house chose the beaten Hebrew over the court that raised him, and it cost him the court. Three weeks of years in Pharaoh's palace ended in a day over one afflicted brother.
cards.s_text: At that time that the war and the siege were against Cush, Moses fled from Egypt from Pharaoh who sought to kill him for having slain the Egyptian.
cards.t_text: And you were three weeks of years at court until the time when you did go forth from the royal court and did see an Egyptian smiting your friend who was of the children of Yashar’el (Israel), and you did slay him and hide him in the sand.

cards.note: *And it came to pass, when the sun had set, that an ecstasy fell upon Abram, and lo! an horror of great darkness fell upon him, and it was said to Abram: “Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land (that is) not theirs, and they will bring them into bondage, and afflict them four hundred years.* (Jubilees 14:13). *For they said the period was completed which Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed to the children of Israel in the times of old, which he had spoken to Abraham.* (Jasher 75:2). Jubilees gives the word to Abram in the darkness: his seed would be strangers in a land not theirs, brought into bondage and afflicted four hundred years. Jasher shows what happened when that word was reckoned wrongly. The children of Ephraim said the period Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed was complete, and went out of Egypt before the time, and the chapter that follows tells of their slaughter. A true word misreckoned kills as surely as a false one. The years were fixed, but they were Yahuah's (God's) to count, and the ones who counted for Him died at the hands of the Philistines.
cards.s_text: For they said the period was completed which Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed to the children of Israel in the times of old, which he had spoken to Abraham.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when the sun had set, that an ecstasy fell upon Abram, and lo! an horror of great darkness fell upon him, and it was said to Abram: “Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land (that is) not theirs, and they will bring them into bondage, and afflict them four hundred years.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:7–8 — *And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar'el (Israel). And Yahuah (God) did everything for Yashar'el's (Israel's) sake, and according to His covenant, which He had ordained with Abraham that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them by force into bondage.* The bodily plague on Pharaoh in Jasher 76:34 foreshadows the ten covenant-judgments Jubilees records on Egypt.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh was ten years afflicted with that plague, still the heart of Pharaoh was more hardened against the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* (Jubilees 48:1). *So Moses went to Midian, for he was afraid to return to Egypt on account of Pharaoh, and he went and sat at a well of water in Midian.* (Jasher 76:13). Jasher gives the first scene of the Midian years, Moses afraid to go back to Egypt, sitting down at a well. Jubilees gives their length, five weeks of years and one year, and the date he went in and the date he came out, down to the week and the jubilee. The one who would stand before Pharaoh spent the better part of his life first as a fugitive at a well. The years are counted so carefully because none of them were wasted; the man who returned in the fiftieth jubilee was not the man who fled in the forty-ninth.
cards.s_text: So Moses went to Midian, for he was afraid to return to Egypt on account of Pharaoh, and he went and sat at a well of water in Midian.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:1 — *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* Jubilees dates Moses' Midian dwelling, the same sojourn in Reuel's house Jasher 77:26 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Moses the son of Amram was still confined in the dungeon in those days, in the house of Reuel the Midianite, and Zipporah the daughter of Reuel did support him with food secretly day by day.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:14 — *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* Jubilees narrates the same Egyptian taskmasters and forced building that Jasher 77:11 says Adikam intensified over Goshen.
cards.s_text: And he placed over them a measure of bricks for them to do according to that number, day by day, and he turned back and went to Egypt.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: *And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel). And Yahuah (God) did everything for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and according to His covenant, which He had ordained with Abraham that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them by force into bondage.* (Jubilees 48:7–8). *And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the cries of the children of Israel, and saw the oppression with which the Egyptians oppressed them.* (Jasher 78:15). Jasher gives the hearing and the seeing: Yahuah (the Lord) heard the cries of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) and saw the oppression. Jubilees gives what came of it, ten great and terrible judgments on Egypt, and says plainly what they were for, vengeance for Yashar'el (Israel) according to the covenant Yahuah (God) had ordained with Abraham. The plagues were not random wrath against a nation; they were a Father keeping an oath sworn four hundred years earlier, that the nation which brought Abraham's seed into bondage by force would be judged for it. He heard, He saw, and then He struck, and every one of the ten came according to the word of Moses.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the cries of the children of Israel, and saw the oppression with which the Egyptians oppressed them.
cards.t_text: And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* (Jubilees 48:1). *In those days Moses, the son of Amram, in Midian, took Zipporah, the daughter of Reuel the Midianite, for a wife.* (Jasher 78:7). Jubilees gives the Midian years in a date, from the forty-ninth jubilee to the fiftieth, five weeks of years and one year. Jasher puts a marriage inside those years, Moses taking Zipporah the daughter of Reuel the Midianite for a wife. The deliverer of Yashar'el (Israel) married outside the camp and kept sheep for a stranger before he ever lifted a rod, and the years are not written as a gap in his story. They are dated to the week because Yahuah (God) was counting them as the preparation of the man.
cards.s_text: In those days Moses, the son of Amram, in Midian, took Zipporah, the daughter of Reuel the Midianite, for a wife.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:2 — *And you yourself know what He spake to you on Mount Sinai, and what prince Mastêmâ desired to do with you when you were returning into Egypt on the way when you did meet him at the lodging-place.* Jubilees names the very lodging-place attack of Jasher 79:8 as the work of Mastêmâ against the returning deliverer.
cards.s_text: And Moses rose up to go to Egypt, and he took his wife and sons with him, and he was at an inn in the road, and an angel of Elohim came down, and sought an occasion against him.
cards.t_text: And you yourself know what He spake to you on Mount Sinai, and what prince Mastêmâ desired to do with you when you were returning into Egypt on the way when you did meet him at the lodging-place.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:3 — *Did he not with all his power seek to slay you and deliver the Egyptians out of your hand when he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and vengeance on the Egyptians?* The deliverance from the inn-angel in Jasher 79:12 is Jubilees' account of Moses rescued from the one who sought to slay him.
cards.s_text: And Zipporah hastened and took of the sharp rock stones that were there, and she circumcised her son, and delivered her husband and her son from the hand of the angel of Yahuah (the Lord).
cards.t_text: Did he not with all his power seek to slay you and deliver the Egyptians out of your hand when he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and vengeance on the Egyptians?

cards.note: Jubilees 48:9 — *And the prince of the Mastêmâ stood up against you, and sought to cast you into the hands of Pharaoh, and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers, and they stood up and wrought before you.* The sorcerers who cast their rods in Jasher 79:37 are, in Jubilees, helped by Mastêmâ to work before Moses.
cards.s_text: And the sorcerers saw this and they cast each man his rod upon the ground and they became serpents.
cards.t_text: And the prince of the Mastêmâ stood up against you, and sought to cast you into the hands of Pharaoh, and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers, and they stood up and wrought before you.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:5 — *And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies... and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.* The plagues that begin to be promised in Jasher 79:55 are Jubilees' great covenant vengeance on Egypt and her idols.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) said to Moses, Behold you will see that with an outstretched hand and heavy plagues, Pharaoh will send the children of Israel from his land.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones, thereby He destroyed everything that grew for them; and by locusts which devoured the residue which had been left by the hail, and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals, and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:4 — *And I delivered you out of his hand, and you did perform the signs and wonders which you were sent to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh, and against all his house, and against his servants and his people.* Jubilees names the same sending against Pharaoh and his subjects that Jasher 80:2 records.
cards.s_text: And Moses went and came to the house of Pharaoh, and he spoke to him the words of Yahuah (the Lord) who had sent him, but Pharaoh would not hearken to the voice of Yahuah (the Lord), and Elohim (God) roused his might in Egypt upon Pharaoh and his subjects, and Elohim smote Pharaoh and his people with very great and sore plagues.
cards.t_text: And I delivered you out of his hand, and you did perform the signs and wonders which you were sent to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh, and against all his house, and against his servants and his people.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:5 — *And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar'el's (Israel's) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones, thereby He destroyed everything that grew for them; and by locusts which devoured the residue which had been left by the hail, and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals, and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.* Jubilees catalogs the same plague-sequence — pestilence on the cattle included — that Jasher 80:24-27 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Elohim sent the pestilence, and the pestilence pervaded Egypt, in the horses and asses, and in the camels, in herds of oxen and sheep and in man.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones, thereby He destroyed everything that grew for them; and by locusts which devoured the residue which had been left by the hail, and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals, and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.

cards.note: Jubilees 49:3 — *And this is the sign which Yahuah (God) gave them: Into every house on the lintels of which they saw the blood of a lamb of the first year, into (that) house they should not enter to slay, but should pass by (it), that all those should be saved that were in the house because the sign of the blood was on its lintels.* Jubilees keeps the same blood-sign Passover Jasher 80:41 commands.
cards.s_text: And the days of darkness passed away, and Yahuah (the Lord) sent Moses and Aaron to the children of Israel, saying, Celebrate your feast and make your Passover, for behold I come in the midst of the night amongst all the Egyptians, and I will smite all their first born, from the first born of a man to the first born of a beast, and when I see your Passover, I will pass over you.
cards.t_text: And this is the sign which Yahuah (God) gave them: Into every house on the lintels of which they saw the blood of a lamb of the first year, into (that) house they should not enter to slay, but should pass by (it), that all those should be saved that were in the house because the sign of the blood was on its lintels.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:7–8 — *And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar'el (Israel). And Yahuah (God) did everything for Yashar'el's (Israel's) sake, and according to His covenant, which He had ordained with Abraham that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them by force into bondage.* Jubilees counts the same ten judgments Moses tallies in Jasher 80:51.
cards.s_text: And Moses said to her, Surely ten plagues did Yahuah (the Lord) bring upon Egypt; did any evil accrue to you from any of them? did one of them affect you? and she said, No.
cards.t_text: And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Jubilees 48:14 — *And all the peoples whom he brought to pursue after Yashar'el (Israel), Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) cast them into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss beneath the children of Yashar'el (Israel)...* Jubilees narrates the same sinking host that Jasher 81:40 says sank in the water.
cards.s_text: And when the children of Israel had entered the sea, the Egyptians came after them, and the waters of the sea resumed upon them, and they all sank in the water, and not one man was left excepting Pharaoh, who gave thanks to Yahuah (the Lord) and believed in him, therefore Yahuah (the Lord) did not cause him to perish at that time with the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: And all the peoples whom he brought to pursue after Yashar’el (Israel), Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) cast them into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss beneath the children of Yashar’el (Israel), even as the people of Egypt had cast their children into the river. He took vengeance on 1,000,000 of them, and one thousand strong and energetic men were destroyed on account of one suckling of the children of your people which they had thrown into the river.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:12–13 — *the prince of the Mastêmâ ... cried to the Egyptians to pursue after you with all the powers of the Egyptians, with their chariots, and with their horses ... And I stood between the Egyptians and Yashar'el (Israel), and we delivered Yashar'el (Israel) out of his hand ... and Yahuah (God) brought them through the midst of the sea as if it were dry land.* Jubilees tells the same pursuit that overtakes Israel at the sea in Jasher 81:24.
cards.s_text: And the whole of this camp went and pursued the children of Israel to bring them back to Egypt, and they reached them encamping by the Red Sea.
cards.t_text: And notwithstanding all (these) signs and wonders the prince of the Mastêmâ was not put to shame because he took courage and cried to the Egyptians to pursue after you with all the powers of the Egyptians, with their chariots, and with their horses, and with all the hosts of the peoples of Egypt.

cards.note: *And we did not lead forth the children of Yashar’el (Israel) from Egypt empty handed.* (Jubilees 48:19). *And at the end of two hundred and ten years, Yahuah (the Lord) brought forth the children of Israel from Egypt with a strong hand.* (Jasher 81:4). The we of Jubilees is the Angel of the Presence speaking, telling Moses that they did not bring the children of Yashar'el (Israel) out of Egypt empty handed. Jasher gives the same going out in its sum, two hundred and ten years ended and Yahuah (the Lord) bringing them out with a strong hand. Angels led and the strong hand of Yahuah (the Lord) drove, and the people walked out carrying the wages of their bondage. The bondage was real and the years were counted, and when the counting was done they left as a nation paid, not as slaves escaped.
cards.s_text: And at the end of two hundred and ten years, Yahuah (the Lord) brought forth the children of Israel from Egypt with a strong hand.
cards.t_text: And we did not lead forth the children of Yashar’el (Israel) from Egypt empty handed.

cards.note: Jubilees 1:1 — *...as Yahuah (God) spake to Moses on Mount Sinai when he went up to receive the tables of the law and of the commandment... in the first year of the exodus... in the third month... “Come up to Me on the Mount, and I will give you two tables of stone of the law and of the commandment, which I have written, that you may teach them.”* Jubilees tells the same third-month Sinai giving Jasher 82:6 records.
cards.s_text: And in the third month from the children of Israel’s departure from Egypt, on the sixth day of it, Yahuah (the Lord) gave to Israel the ten commandments on Mount Sinai.
cards.t_text: This is the history of the division of the days of the law and of the testimony, of the events of the years, of their (year) weeks, of their jubilees throughout all the years of the world, as Yahuah (God) spake to Moses on Mount Sinai when he went up to receive the tables of the law and of the commandment, according to the voice of Elohim (God) as He said to him, “Go up to the top of the Mount.” And it came to pass in the first year of the exodus of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) out of Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of the month, that Elohim (God) spake to Moses, saying: “Come up to Me on the Mount, and I will give you two tables of stone of the law and of the commandment, which I have written, that you may teach them.”

cards.note: Jubilees 1:4 — *And Moses was on the Mount forty days and forty nights, and Elohim (God) taught him the earlier and the later history of the division of all the days of the law and of the testimony.* the same forty days of instruction Jasher 82:9 gives as statutes and judgments to teach Israel.
cards.s_text: And Moses was upon the mount forty days and forty nights; he ate no bread and drank no water, and Yahuah (the Lord) instructed him in the statutes and judgments in order to teach the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: And Moses was on the Mount forty days and forty nights, and Elohim (God) taught him the earlier and the later history of the division of all the days of the law and of the testimony.

cards.note: *And the king of Egypt went forth to war with the king of Canaan in the forty-seventh jubilee, in the second week in the second year, and the children of Yashar’el (Israel) brought forth all the bones of the children of Jacob save the bones of Joseph, and they buried them in the field in the double cave in the mountain.* (Jubilees 46:9). *And it was in those days, when the children of Israel were dwelling securely in their cities, that they buried the coffins of the tribes of their ancestors, which they had brought up from Egypt, each man in the inheritance of his children, the twelve sons of Jacob did the children of Israel bury, each man in the possession of his children.* (Jasher 90:38). Both witnesses agree the sons of Jacob did not stay in Egypt's ground; they differ on when their bones went home. Jubilees has them carried up early, while the king of Egypt was off at war with Canaan, and laid in the double cave in the mountain, all but Joseph. Jasher has the coffins carried up out of Egypt at the exodus and buried after the land had rest, each man in the inheritance of his own children. Either way the fathers were waiting for the land and were brought into it. Joseph alone, in Jubilees' telling, had to wait for the whole nation to come out with him.
cards.s_text: And it was in those days, when the children of Israel were dwelling securely in their cities, that they buried the coffins of the tribes of their ancestors, which they had brought up from Egypt, each man in the inheritance of his children, the twelve sons of Jacob did the children of Israel bury, each man in the possession of his children.
cards.t_text: And the king of Egypt went forth to war with the king of Canaan in the forty-seventh jubilee, in the second week in the second year, and the children of Yashar’el (Israel) brought forth all the bones of the children of Jacob save the bones of Joseph, and they buried them in the field in the double cave in the mountain.

cards.note: *For all the land which you see I shall give to you and to your seed for ever, and I shall make your seed as the sand of the sea: though a man may number the dust of the earth, yet your seed shall not be numbered.* (Jubilees 13:20). *And Yahuah (the Lord) gave to the children of Israel the whole land of Canaan, as he had sworn to their ancestors, and Yahuah (the Lord) gave them rest from those around them, and the children of Israel dwelt securely in their cities.* (Jasher 91:15). Jubilees gives the promise to Abram as he stood looking at the land: all of it to him and to his seed for ever, and a seed past counting. Jasher gives the receipt generations later, Yahuah (the Lord) giving the children of Yashar'el (Israel) the whole land of Canaan as he had sworn to their ancestors, and rest from those around them. The oath was to a man and his bloodline, and it was kept to the bloodline. The word in Jubilees is for ever, which means the land grant did not expire with Joshua or with any later exile; the same seed is still the heir.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) gave to the children of Israel the whole land of Canaan, as he had sworn to their ancestors, and Yahuah (the Lord) gave them rest from those around them, and the children of Israel dwelt securely in their cities.
cards.t_text: For all the land which you see I shall give to you and to your seed for ever, and I shall make your seed as the sand of the sea: though a man may number the dust of the earth, yet your seed shall not be numbered.

cards.note: The Book of Jubilees 4:23 — *And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour, and behold there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men.* Jubilees narrates the very taking-away from among men that Wisdom of Solomon 4:11 says spared Enoch from wickedness.
cards.s_text: Yea speedily was he taken away, lest that wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.
cards.t_text: And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour, and behold there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:14 — *And all the peoples whom he brought to pursue after Yashar'el (Israel), Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) cast them into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss beneath the children of Yashar'el (Israel), even as the people of Egypt had cast their children into the river. He took vengeance on 1,000,000 of them, and one thousand strong and energetic men were destroyed on account of one suckling of the children of your people which they had thrown into the river.* The now-live Jubilees self-links Wisdom who *drowned their enemies, and cast them up out of the bottom of the deep* (10:19).
cards.s_text: But she drowned their enemies, and cast them up out of the bottom of the deep.
cards.t_text: And all the peoples whom he brought to pursue after Yashar’el (Israel), Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) cast them into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss beneath the children of Yashar’el (Israel), even as the people of Egypt had cast their children into the river. He took vengeance on 1,000,000 of them, and one thousand strong and energetic men were destroyed on account of one suckling of the children of your people which they had thrown into the river.

cards.note: Jubilees 39:3 — *And he set Joseph over all his house, and the blessing of Yahuah (God) came upon the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph, and Yahuah (God) prospered him in all that he did.* The now-live Jubilees self-links Wisdom who *delivered him from sin* and went down into the pit (10:13).
cards.s_text: When the righteous was sold, she forsook him not, but delivered him from sin: she went down with him into the pit,
